talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: My nose runs and I feel hot.
That sounds like a cold. Do you have a headache?
Yes, my head hurts a lot.
Drink some warm water. Are you able to sleep?
I am very tired but cannot sleep well.
Rest is good for you.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I found a bright red leaf on the ground today.
That sounds nice. What did you do with it?
I put it in my pocket to keep.
I do not know why it matters, but it seems special.
It made me smile for the rest of the day.
I am glad you are happy.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: The rain was very loud today at my meeting.
That sounds scary to listen to. Did you have an umbrella with you?
No, I forgot it at home, so I got a little wet.
Oh no, I am sorry you got wet. It is good that you are dry now.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why are you late?
The red light stuck me. Are you in a hurry?
Yes, we need to go now.
Sorry, I am running. Can you walk faster?
Why did the light stay red?
I do not know for sure. Do we still have time?
Just barely, I think.
Okay, let us move.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: The sky is very gray and the ground is wet. I do not know where to go.
That can feel heavy. Do you have a cozy blanket at home?
Yes, I have a big blue one. But I am not sure if I want to stay in.
You can always go outside later. Is the rain loud right now?
It is just a soft drip. I think I will sit by the window and watch it fall.
That sounds like a good plan.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Is that a lake?
Yes, that is a lake. Do you see the water?
What is in the lake?
It has water and fish. Is there a boat?
Is the water deep?
It can be very deep. Why do you ask?
Can I swim in it?
Only if an adult is there. Do you like swimming?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I am not sure what to put in my bag.
What is the bag for?
It is for a trip to the beach.
Pack your swimsuit. Did you bring a towel?
I forgot the towel. Do I need a book?
A book is good for fun. Do you like to swim?
Yes, I do. Should I pack snacks?
Snacks are a good idea. Have a nice day!

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I want to clean my room, but I do not know where to start.
A good place to start is the floor. Do you have a broom?
I have a broom, but I do not know how to use it.
Just sweep the dirt to one side. Is your bed also messy?
Yes, my bed is very messy and I feel tired.
Put the clothes on a chair first. Then rest a little.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am so tired but my brain will not stop.
Try to count your breaths slowly. Do you have a soft pillow?
Yes, it is very soft, but I feel hot.
A cold room helps you sleep. Is it warm in your room?
It is warm. I need to fix this now.
Open the window a little. I hope you feel cool soon.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am sad because the old well in our village is broken.
That is a sad thing. Why is the well so important to you?
My favorite cat always drinks from it at noon.
I understand your worry. Did anyone try to fix the stones?
No, the village elders say they will wait for rain.
Patience can be hard. Do you have another plan to help the cat?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I have a toy boat. It does not float. What do I do?
Try adding weight to the middle. Do you have any small pebbles?
No, just paper. How does a real ship stay up?
Big ships push water out to stay up. Is your boat very light?
Yes, it is light. But it still sinks fast.
Check for small holes in the bottom. Do you see water inside?
No holes. I think I gave up.
Water is very strong. You did your best.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I see a big color band in the sky. Where did it come from?
It made when sun shines on wet air. Do you see red?
Yes, red is top. I have to run now.
Run safe. The colors do not move. Do you like blue?
Blue is nice. I must go.
Goodbye. Tell me what you find next.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am sad because I forgot the month after May.
That can feel very hard. Do you remember what comes right after April?
Yes, it is May, but I cannot fix the gap.
It is June. How do you feel about learning it now?
I think I can try if you help me.
I believe you can do it. Would you like to list the first three months?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: Look at the clock! It is three o'clock.
Wow, that is a nice time. Do you like the number three?
Yes, I do. It means snack time.
Snacks sound very good. What is your favorite treat?
I love cookies. They are sweet and round.
Cookies are a great choice. Do you have any right now?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I see smoke near the house.
Is it a big fire or a small one?
I need to go help now.
Stay safe. Do you know who lives there?
The door is stuck.
Try to open it. Can you see the people inside?
I am leaving now.
Call for help if you are scared.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: The sky is so blue today! I love looking up at it.
It is lovely, isn't it? Do you know why it looks that way?
I think it is because the sun is happy and shining bright!
That is a sweet thought, but it is not the real reason. I do know the truth, though.
Oh, tell me! Why is the sky blue?
Sunlight mixes with air and spreads out. It scatters the blue color all over the dome above us.
Wow, that is so cool! It makes me feel very happy.
I am glad it makes you smile. Do you plan to stay outside and look up again?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: Can I swim in the big lake?
Only if you have a grown-up watching you close by. Is the water warm or cold?
It looks cold, like ice.
That means we must be very careful. Do you have your swimsuit on?
No, I am wearing my socks.
Then we should walk on the grass instead. Do you see any ducks?
Yes, there is one floating there.
It looks very happy. What color is its beak?
It is orange and yellow.
Nature is full of bright colors. Do you want to see more birds?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I stop my bike without falling?
You use the brakes to slow down. Do you know which hand uses which brake?
I push the right lever for the front wheel.
That is a good start. Now, how do you feel when you pull it hard?
It feels scary because I might flip over.
Keep your eyes up, not down. Have you tried practicing on a gentle slope?
I only ride on flat ground at the park.
Flat ground is safe for beginners. Do you have a friend to watch you?
No, I am always alone when I ride.
That can be lonely. Would you like to start by just putting one foot on the ground while stopping?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do we help our friends?
Because it makes them feel safe and happy. Do you like to make people smile?
I do like that. Why do you do it?
I do it because I care. What do you do to help?
I share my toys. Why is sharing good?
Sharing shows love and builds trust. Do you think that is fair?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I need to find my old friend Sam. Do you know where he lives?
I do not know his house, but I do know he likes parks. Do you see a park nearby?
No, I do not see one. I must go now.
That is good to hear. Is your bag with you?
Yes, my bag is here. I am going.
Have a safe trip. Good luck.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I found a bug in my room. What should I do?
Do not squash it. Is it small or large?
It is small and black. I am scared of it.
That is good. It is likely just a little beetle. Do you have a glass?
Yes, I do. Where is my glass?
Use the glass to trap it gently. Then, carry it outside.
I put it outside. Thank you.
You did a good job. Nature is safe again.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why do magnets stick to some things and not others?
They only stick to iron and steel. Do you have a big fridge in your kitchen?
Yes, I have one with lots of pictures on it.
The fridge door is made of metal that magnets love. Did you try putting a magnet on a wooden table?
No, because I know it would not stay.
That is very smart. Do you like making things with magnets?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why does my dog wag his tail when I come home?
He wags his tail because he is happy to see you. Do you pet him?
Yes, I do. Why does he lick my face?
Licking is how dogs say they love you. Do you like it?
I do. Why does he bark at the cat?
I do not know for sure why he barks at that specific cat.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I just found a bakery with the best warm bread I have ever eaten.
That sounds very happy for you. What kind of bread do you like best?
I love sweet rolls with a soft crust and lots of butter.
A little butter makes everything taste nicer. Do you go there often?
I plan to go back every single week to eat more rolls.
That is a wonderful plan to look forward to.
I just found a bakery with the best warm bread I have ever eaten.
That sounds very happy for you. What kind of bread do you like best?
I love sweet rolls with a soft crust and lots of butter.
A little butter makes everything taste nicer. Do you go there often?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I do not know what to buy here.
That is okay. What do you like to eat?
I want something sweet and cool.
Look for the ice cream stand over there. Do you like chocolate?
Yes, I love chocolate.
Then get the chocolate bar. It will make you happy.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why is the play so funny to me?
It is funny because the actors act in a silly way. Do you like silly things?
Why do they fall down so many times?
They fall down to make you laugh.
Why is the music so loud?
The music is loud to help you feel the story. Is the music too loud for you?
Why is the story sad at the end?
Stories can be sad to show how feelings work.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: The sky turned red this evening because of a fire.
Oh no, that looks scary to see. Did you see the smoke from far away?
Yes, it looked like big gray clouds moving fast.
I am glad you are safe inside. Did the fire stop by now?
It is almost gone, just a little heat left.
That is a good thing to hear.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why is the bread warm?
The oven keeps it hot for you. Do you like warm bread?
Yes, I do. Why is the flour white?
We grind the grain to make it fine. Is that all you wanted to know?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to bake a cake.
That sounds fun. Do you have an oven?
Yes, I do. What do I need first?
You need flour, sugar, eggs, and butter.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to know how to write like people did long ago.
That is a great goal! Do you have a quill?
I have a pen, but I feel silly.
Pens work just fine. Why do you feel silly?
I am afraid my words will look bad.
Practice makes perfect. Let us try a few letters.
Can you show me how to hold it?
I cannot see your hand, but you hold it loosely like a twig.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: My computer makes a loud noise.
Is it a hot hum or a loud beep?
It is a loud beep.
That might mean it needs to cool down.
How do I make it quiet?
You can open a window to let air in.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I dropped my juice cup on the floor. It made a big splash. I said sorry to the floor, but it did not answer.
That is a sweet thing to do. Did you wipe up the mess?
Yes, I used a towel. My mom smiled at me. She said I was being kind.
Your mom is right to be happy. Do you feel better now?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to say "hello" in a new language.
That is a great start. What language do you want to learn?
I just want to be able to greet people kindly.
Saying "hello" is a very kind first step.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late for school. What time is it?
It is ten past eight. Do you have your bag?
I do not see the clock. Is it almost nine?
No, it is ten past eight. Take a deep breath.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: The wind is blowing very hard outside. Is the storm going to stop soon?
I do not know for sure, but it should end before dark. Are your windows shut tight?
Yes, I checked them earlier. Do you think it will get worse?
It might get a bit louder. Do you like the sound of rain on the roof?
I do not, but I am safe inside. Thank you for talking with me.
You are welcome. Stay dry and happy.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I want to read a book in bed at night, but I keep falling asleep.
That is very common. Do you read under bright lights?
Yes, I use a strong lamp, but my eyes feel tired.
Try a soft, warm light instead. It helps you feel sleepy.
That makes sense. How do I stop falling asleep before the end?
You might read only a few pages each night. Is the story exciting for you?
It is a bit boring, which makes me nod off.
Choose a book you love. Fun stories keep you awake.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I found a box with a secret lock. What should I do to open it?
Look for a small key or a code on the box. Do you see any numbers or letters on it?
There are four numbers on the dial. How do I know which ones to turn?
Check if the numbers match a date or a pattern. Is there a picture or a clue nearby?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: My neighbor plays loud music late at night.
That sounds hard to sleep through. Do you know their name?
Yes, but I do not want to be rude.
You can be kind and clear. Have you tried talking to them?
Not yet. I am afraid they will get angry.
Most people like a gentle note. Would you like help writing one?
Yes, please. I will try to stay calm.
That is a good plan. Take your time.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why do some snowflakes look like stars?
Each snowflake builds from ice bits in the air. Do you like how they sparkle?
Yes, I do. Do all snowflakes look the same?
No, they are all unique shapes. Do you like catching them on your tongue?
I tried once and it was cold. Is snow always white?
Mostly yes, but it can look blue in deep drifts. Do you like making snow angels?
I have not made one yet. Can I make one with you?
I cannot come outside, but you can try. Have fun in the snow.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I tried to draw a dog today but it looked like a cat.
That is a funny mix up. What color was the dog?
It was brown, but my pencil broke right in the middle.
Oh no, that is frustrating. Did you find another pencil?
I did, but it was too short to hold well.
That must be hard. Do you like drawing cats more?
I think I do, actually. Cats have easier ears to draw.
That makes sense. What else do you want to draw next?
I want to draw a big tree with many leaves.
That sounds like a great idea. Have a fun time with it.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am sad because the surprise is ruined.
That is a shame. Do you know what broke it?
The box fell and the toy inside is cracked.
I am sorry to hear that.
I wanted to give it to my friend today.
That is a thoughtful gift. What is the toy?
It is a red truck.
A truck is fun. Can we fix the crack?
I do not think we can fix it.
I understand. Let us try another idea.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do we say sorry?
It helps the person you hurt feel better. Do you think words can fix things?
I guess so. What if I do not know why I said sorry?
Then just tell them you care about them. Would you like a simple phrase to use?
Yes, please. How do I start?
Start with "I am sorry for what I did." It shows you are true and kind.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: It is so hot outside. I do not know what to do.
I am glad you asked. Do you like the water?
Yes, but I am too tired to go to the pool.
That sounds hard. Maybe you can just take a cool shower?
That is a good idea. I will do that now.
That is a smart choice.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I think I packed my shoes.
Good, do you have your socks too?
Yes, the blue ones.
Nice pick, what is in the red box?
I do not know.
You can look, but do you have your toy?
The teddy bear is there.
I am glad, do you feel happy?
Yes, it feels light.
Great, let us go.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I want to go to the party.
That sounds like fun. What are you wearing?
I have a red hat.
A red hat is bright. Do you have a snack for the party?
Yes, I have a cookie.
A cookie is a nice treat. Are you nervous about going?
No, I am happy.
Happy is a good feeling. Have a great time.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do people keep all these old papers?
Most of them are just memories of the past. Do you like to keep old things?
I do not, I just throw them out.
That is a simple way to stay clean. I do not know if it saves time for you.
It saves me a lot of space in my home.
A tidy home feels very good. What is the first thing you clean?
I start with my desk because I work there.
A clear desk helps your mind work well.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I feel very alone. I want to learn how to play the guitar, but I am not sure how to start.
That is a wonderful idea. Do you have a guitar already?
No, I do not have one yet. I just want to know how to make the first sound.
You can strum the strings gently. How does that sound to you?
I am not sure. I am afraid I will break it.
You will not break it if you are soft. Do you like soft music?
Yes, I like it. I am still feeling lonely, though. Can you promise to stay with me while I try?
I am here with you right now. Try one soft strum and tell me how it feels.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Is my teacher nice?
Yes, she is very kind. Do you like her?
Sometimes she is loud.
I understand that feeling. Is it too loud?
It hurts my ears.
Tell her that, please.
I will try to talk to her.
That is a good idea.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: My computer works so well today. I am very happy about it.
That is great news. Do you play games on it?
Yes, I play many fun games. I want to tell everyone.
Share your joy. Is the screen bright and clear?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why do bears eat bugs?
They dig in the ground for food. Do you like to dig?
I guess so. Is a penguin a bird?
Yes, it flies in the water but not the air. Do you like the sea?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: I like that book. Why do you like it?
It makes me smile. Do you have a favorite story?
I think it is kind. Why is it special to you?
It reminds me of my home. Does it make you happy?
The words are soft. Why do they feel nice?
I am not sure why, but I love them. Do you read it at night?
Yes, before bed. What does it show you?
It shows me quiet peace. Do you feel calm too?
I do, every time. Why does it stay with you?
It is a good friend. Do you keep it safe?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: The noise here makes my head hurt.
That feels bad. Do you like quiet places?
I just want to sit down and rest.
I do not know where you are. Is there a park nearby?
I am too tired to look for one.
Maybe you can sit right here. Does the wind feel nice?
It helps a little, thank you.
I am glad you feel better. Do you like the smell of the flowers?
Yes, they smell sweet.
Sweet smells help us feel calm. Are you ready to walk now?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: How do I draw a round sun?
Try to trace a circle. Are you using a pencil or a crayon?
I use a crayon. It feels hard to make it round.
Move your wrist, not your whole arm. That helps a lot.
Oh, that worked! Now the sun is not too big.
Great job. Do you want to add some rays next?
Yes, please. How long should the rays be?
Short lines look cute and neat.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I am not sure what to put in my bag for the trip.
Bring some clothes and a book. Do you like to read?
Yes, I love stories, but I forgot my lunch.
You should pack a sandwich and some fruit.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: My bread is getting very big and puffy today. I put it in a warm spot.
That is nice to hear. Does it smell sweet to you?
Yes, it smells like dinner. Why does the dough get big?
Tiny bugs in the flour make gas bubbles. Do you see them?
I see little holes, not bugs. I am glad it is working.
You are right, the holes are from the gas. It is a happy day.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I like my book about the bear.
Bears are funny. What does yours do?
He eats too much honey.
That sounds sweet. Do you like bears?
Yes. His name is Barnaby.
Barnaby is a nice name. Is he happy?
He is. But he feels tired.
He needs a nap. Do you have a nap?
Yes. I sleep on my rug.
That sounds cozy.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why does the ball go back and forth?
The players hit it with their rackets. Do you play often?
I play a little bit.
That is fun. Do you like the serve?
I hate the serve because it is hard.
That is normal. Everyone finds it tricky at first.
How do I get better?
Just keep playing and having fun. Will you practice again soon?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I am not sure which bus to take.
What street is your home on?
It is on Main Street.
You need bus number five. Is it raining outside?
No, the sun is very bright.
Take the walk to the stop.
Thank you for your help.
You are welcome. Have a safe trip.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I love the library. It is so quiet and cozy.
That is a great place. Do you read there?
Yes, I read many books. The shelves are full of stories.
What book is your favorite?
It is a book about a dog. I feel very happy when I read it.
Dogs are good friends. Is the dog brave?
Yes, he is very brave. I want to visit again tomorrow.
You should go. Will you go now?
I will go this weekend. Thank you for talking to me.
You are welcome. Have fun.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: My dog ran away. I must go.
Oh no. Is he near the park?
He likes the park. I am late.
Do not worry. I will look there.
Thank you. Goodbye.
Be safe. Come back soon.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: How do I keep my balance on the bike?
Look far ahead, not at your feet. Is your bike big enough for you?
Yes, my feet touch the ground.
That is good. Start by walking the bike first. Do you have a helmet on?
I am wearing one.
Smart. Now lift your front tire and push. Did you take a small hop?
I did, but I wobbled.
That is normal. Keep your hands light on the bars. Can you see a straight path to ride on?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do we eat in the big room?
It is quiet there. Do you like the quiet?
Yes, it feels nice. Why do you bring soup every day?
I made it at home. Do you like soup?
I do. Why is the bread brown?
It was baked in the heat. I do not know why it is that color.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I saw a big brown bear in the park today.
That is amazing. What did the bear do?
It was just eating berries under a tree.
I am so happy you are safe. Did you take a picture?
I could not because my hands were full of snacks.
You must tell me what you ate. Was it cold?
Yes, it was ice cream and I love it.
That sounds very sweet.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late. Why do bees buzz?
They move their wings fast. Do you like honey?
Yes, it is sweet. How many legs do ants have?
They have six legs. Do you see any outside?
I am running. I cannot see any.
They are small. Be safe on your way.
Thank you. I must go now.
You are welcome. I hope you arrive on time.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I lost my ring.
Oh no. Did you look in your pocket?
Yes, but it is not there.
That is bad. Did you give it to your mom?
No, I kept it on my finger.
We must find it. Where did you last take it off?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I feel very scared about the big test tomorrow.
That is a big feeling. Do you want to talk about it?
My hands shake when I study.
That shows you care. Have you eaten a snack yet?
Yes, I had cookies.
Good. I do not know what is on the test.
It is hard. I might fail.
That is a scary thought. Do you have a plan for studying?
I will try my best.
That is brave. You can do this.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to fix my old bike like my friend did.
That sounds fun. Did you pack a tool kit?
I have a wrench, but I do not know where to start.
Start with the brakes. Do they feel loose?
Yes, they are very soft.
Tighten the little screw with a coin. Can you find the coin?
I found it, but the wheel is wobbly.
That is tricky. I do not know the exact trick for that.
Please help me with the wobbly wheel.
Check the spokes for slack. Are any bending?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why does the light on the tower spin?
It spins so the beam can be seen from far away. Do you have a favorite color for lights?
I like blue. Is the keeper alone in the dark?
Yes, but he has friends like cats and books to keep him happy.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to see the bright light in the sky. How can I do that?
Just step outside during the day. Do you like looking up?
Yes, but it feels very hot on my skin. How can I stay cool?
Wear a hat and drink some water. Do you have a hat nearby?
I do, and I feel much better now. Is that all there is to it?
Yes, that is all you need.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am very late. My bus is coming.
That sounds scary. Do you have your bag?
Yes, I have it. Please do not block the door.
I am stepping aside. Good luck on your trip.
Thank you. I must run now.
Run safe. What is the job you are late for?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I moved my king today and felt so proud.
That is a big step. Did you keep him safe?
Yes, I hid him behind my wall of pawns.
Smart move. How did the other player react?
They looked very sad and stopped talking.
That is a sad face. Do you play often?
Only on weekends with my uncle.
Nice time together.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I feel very sick and cold.
That sounds rough. Do you have a fever?
Yes, my head feels hot and heavy.
Please drink warm water. Is it hard to breathe?
Not really, just tired and achy.
Rest is the best cure. Have you eaten?
Not since yesterday, my stomach hurts.
Try some plain rice. That helps.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why do the birds sing every morning?
They sing to show their spot is safe. Do you like the sound?
Yes, it is very pretty.
It helps them find friends too. Do you see any red ones?
I see some brown ones on the wire.
Those are likely robins.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I want to bake a bread. How do I start?
Mix flour, water, salt, and yeast in a bowl. Do you have fresh yeast?
Yes, I have the fresh kind. What do I do next?
Stir it well and let it sit for an hour. It will double in size.
It is getting big. Now what?
Shape it and put it on a pan. Is your oven ready?
The oven is hot. How long do I bake it?
Bake for twenty to thirty minutes until it sounds hollow. You should be proud of your work.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I need to find the main beach path fast.
Go straight ahead. Is it very windy?
Yes, please tell me where the bathrooms are.
They are on the left. Do you like sand?
I am running, so tell me the way to the pier.
Turn right past the shop.
I am late, so is the gate open?
I do not know.
Thank you, I must go now.
Good luck.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to know how to pick the right shoe size.
Try them on in the evening when feet are big. Do you usually wear socks with your shoes?
Yes, I always wear thick socks.
That is smart. Your toes should have a little space to wiggle.
What if one foot feels tight?
Pick the size that fits the bigger foot. Do you have a tape measure at home?
No, I do not have a tape.
Put your foot on a piece of paper and mark the heel and toes. The distance between the marks is your size.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I like the cold and snow. Which season is that?
That is winter. Do you like to build snowmen?
Yes, I love snowmen. What comes after winter?
Spring comes next when flowers grow.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I do not know what to do with my book.
That is okay. Did you finish the story?
Yes, I read it all the way to the end.
Good work. Do you like the characters?
I like the little dog, but I am not sure what to do next.
You can read it again. Do you want to share it with a friend?
I think I will just put it on my shelf for now.
That is a good choice. I hope you enjoy it more later.
Thank you, that helps me feel better.
You are welcome. Reading is always a good thing.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: My neighbour keeps loud music at night. I do not know what to do.
That is very tiring. Have you tried talking to them?
I am afraid they will be angry.
It is smart to be careful. Do you know who lives above you?
I think so, but I am not sure.
Try a polite knock first. I hope it works!

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I got lost on my way home from school today.
That can be scary. Did you stay close to the main street?
Yes, I just walked until I saw a big red building.
Good idea. Was it a store or a library?
It was the bakery where I like to buy cookies.
That is a very safe place. You are smart to go there.
The baker let me call my mom from his phone.
I am glad your mom came to get you. Are you hungry now?
Not really, but I am very tired.
That makes sense. You can rest now.
Thank you for listening to my story.
I am happy to help. I do not know more, but I am glad you are safe.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I found a puzzle piece that does not fit. What is it?
That is odd. Did you try turning it around?
I tried turning it, but it still will not go in.
Maybe it belongs to another puzzle? Check the other box.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I am so late for school.
Oh no. Did you forget your backpack?
No, but my shoes were in the wrong room.
That is tricky. Do you have time for a snack?
No, I have to go now.
Okay, good luck. Can you run safely?
Yes, I will be careful.
Great. I hope you make it on time.
Thanks for helping me.
You are welcome. I am glad you are okay.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do people sing?
Singing makes your heart feel warm and happy. Do you like happy songs?
Yes, I do. How do I start?
You just open your mouth and let sound come out. Do you have a favorite song?
I like old songs. Is it hard?
No, it is easy if you just try. Do you want to try now?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I see the sky is blue, but I do not know why.
Sunlight has many colors. Blue light bounces around more than other colors. What color is the grass to you?
I see green grass, but I am still unsure about the blue sky.
The air scatters the blue light to our eyes. That is why we see blue overhead. Do you like looking up?
I understand now, thanks to your kind help.
I am happy it made sense to you. You learned something new today.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I am very tired. The street is too loud.
That sounds hard. Do you like the cold air?
No, it is warm. I do not know where to sit.
A bench near the trees would be good. Do you see one?
Yes, I do. It looks quiet.
Good. Sit down and rest.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I just moved to a small, sunny town.
That sounds lovely. Do you have a favorite place there?
Yes, the big oak tree by the park.
An oak tree? That must be quite old and strong.
It is. My kids love to climb it.
How wonderful for them to play. Is it safe for them?
It is, because there is a soft grassy hill below.
That is good. Do you like the quiet streets?
I do. It feels like a happy dream.
I am glad you are happy there. I know little else, but your joy is clear.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: My old friend lives far away.
Is that a sad thought?
I do not know what to do.
You could just call him.
But I have no number.
Do you have his letter?
I lost it long ago.
Then we must think of other ways.
I feel very lost.
That is okay. We go step by step.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I met a new friend today. He is very quiet.
That is nice. Do you like talking to him?
Yes, but I do not know his name yet.
Oh, that is strange. Would you like to ask him?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am so tired. The city is too loud and too fast.
It can be very stressful there. Do you like the noise?
No, I hate it. I miss the quiet of my home.
That sounds like a good place to rest. Are you going home soon?
Yes, I am leaving tonight. Thank you for listening.
I hope you have a peaceful ride.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I miss the bus. What do I do?
Oof, that is bad news. Do you have a phone?
Yes, I do. Where do I go now?
Go to the next stop. Wait there for the next bus.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I found three red buttons on my shirt today.
That is a lucky find. How did you feel?
I felt very happy and proud of my pocket.
It is nice to keep small treasures. Do you keep them all?
Yes, I put them in a small blue box.
A blue box is a perfect home. What else is in the box?
I also have a shiny coin and a single feather.
Those are special items. I do not know where you found the coin.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I bought so many red roses today because I feel so happy.
That is wonderful to hear. What made you choose red ones?
I just love how they look bright and warm in the sun.
They must look very pretty. Do you have a special vase for them?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I feel lost. I do not know what to say to the bride.
That is a normal feeling. Have you asked her favorite color?
I do not know. I just want to do the right thing.
Being nice is the right thing. Do you have a big hug ready?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I am so late. What can I do?
Run to the door now. Do you have your keys?
Yes, I have them. I feel very bad.
It is okay to make mistakes. Are you safe?
I am fine. I just miss the bus.
That is a small problem. Do not worry.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I take a piece?
You just move your piece to where the other piece is. Do you know how to start the game?
Yes, but how do I win?
You win by trapping the king so it cannot move. Do you have a board yet?
I do. Thanks for the help.
You are welcome. Have fun playing.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am so sad that my bird feeder is empty again.
That sounds tough. Do you know where your birds go?
I think they just fly away and forget me.
They likely want to find more food. What kind of seeds do you usually use?
Sunflower seeds, but they are expensive.
I do not know a cheaper brand. Have you tried putting out bread?
I heard bread is bad for them.
You are right, bread is not good. It is sweet that you care about them.
So I just have to buy more seeds?
Yes, buying more is the safe choice. Do you like watching them eat?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: I want to sleep well. Why does a dark room help?
Darkness tells your body to rest. Do you like reading in bed?
Yes, I do. But why does that keep me awake?
Light tricks your brain into thinking it is day. I am not sure if it hurts your eyes.
That makes sense. Why is a cool room good for sleep?
A lower temperature helps your body relax. Do you use a heavy blanket?
Sometimes. Why does that feel so good?
The weight gives you a feeling of safety. I do not know why it works for everyone.
I understand now. Why do I need a set time to sleep?
Your body likes a steady clock. Do you wake up at the same time?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to make good coffee. How do I do it?
Just use hot water and fresh coffee powder. Do you like it sweet?
Yes, I do. How much sugar is best?
Start with one spoon and taste it.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I feel so alone right now, but I have to rush.
I am sorry you feel that way. Do you have a friend nearby?
No, I must go.
I care about you.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I feel very happy today.
That is wonderful to hear. What made you feel this way?
The sun is out and the sky is blue.
Nature is a great gift. Do you like the warm light?
Yes, it feels good on my face.
I am glad you enjoy it.
I just wanted to share this joy.
You are very kind to tell me.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to make a paper boat. Can you help me?
Sure, I can help. What kind of paper do you have?
I have a green sheet. Where do I start?
Fold the top corners to the middle first. Do you have a flat table?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: The wind is so loud and I am scared. What should I do?
It is very scary when the storm is loud. Do you have a warm blanket with you?
Yes, I have a blanket, but the lights are going out. Is it safe?
Yes, it is safe to stay in a dry room. Please stay away from the windows.
Okay, I will sit on the bed with my blanket. What else can I do?
I do not know for sure, but reading a book might help. Is your book fun?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Do you have any food that is safe for my cat?
I do not sell food for cats. Do you like fish?
No, I only care about the cat.
I cannot help with that question. I am sorry.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I put my dough in the warm spot and went for a walk.
That sounds like a nice break. Did you check on it when you got back?
I came home and the dough was twice as big. It looked so soft.
Warmth helps the tiny workers eat the sugar. Do you know what they are called?
I think they are yeast, but I am not sure. Can you tell me?
Yes, it is yeast. They make air bubbles to lift the bread up.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I saw a big blue whale in the museum today.
That must have been very cool. Did you touch the whale?
No, it was behind glass, but I looked inside its mouth.
How scary that must have been. Was it dark in there?
It was a little dark, but I saw a lot of sharp teeth.
Wow, that is quite a lot of teeth. Do you like animals?
I like big animals the best. I want to go back next week.
That sounds like a great plan. Have a happy day.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I feel very sad inside today.
I am sorry you feel that way. What made you feel this way?
My toy broke and I cannot fix it.
That is a hard thing to accept. Are you angry about it too?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I tried to sleep but my mind kept spinning about the big test I have tomorrow.
That feels scary. Do you want to talk about what you are worried about?
I am afraid I will get a bad grade because I did not study enough last night.
It is okay to feel nervous. I do not know your test, but I can help you plan.
I will try to write down my questions now to stop the spinning in my head.
That sounds like a good plan. Did you eat a light snack before bed?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: My boss gave me a hard book on knots. I want to learn the knot that looks like a bow.
That sounds like a great start. Do you have the right kind of rope on hand?
Yes, I have a red rope. But I am not sure where to start with the first loop.
You just make a simple loop with the short end. Do you want to try that first?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: My little fish is sitting at the bottom and not moving. I feel sad.
I am sorry to hear that. Is the water clean and cool?
Yes, I changed it yesterday, but he still looks tired.
That is good that the water is fresh. How much did you feed him today?
I gave him lots of flakes because he seemed hungry.
Too much food can make fish sick. Try waiting one day to feed him again.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I lost my toy on the island and I feel sad.
I am sorry. Do you know where you were playing?
I was near the big tree but the tide took it.
That is a hard thing to lose. Have you asked your friend to help look?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I make a sandwich?
Put bread on the plate. Do you like cheese?
Yes, I love cheese.
Put the cheese on the bottom bread. What else is on your plate?
I have some tomatoes.
Cut the tomatoes and put them on top. Do you want to add butter?
No, just the tomato.
Place the top bread on the stack. Is that clear?
Yes, I will try it now.
Good luck with your snack.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: My bike tire is flat and I am so mad.
That is very frustrating. Do you have a pump?
I do not have a pump or a patch.
That is hard to fix right now. I do not know what to do.
I just need to get to school on time.
I am sorry you feel stuck. Are you close to home?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am very happy today because I saw a bear!
That is wonderful to hear! Did the bear look big?
Yes, it was huge and brown, and it just sat there.
It must have been a cool sight. Do you like bears?
I do, but I know they are wild and can be scary.
That is a good thing to know. It is best to watch from far away.
I will tell you more about my trip soon!
I would like that. What is your next stop?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I have a blank canvas and no idea what to paint.
That is okay. What color makes you feel happy?
Blue, I think. But I am still stuck.
Try painting a blue sky. Can you see the sun?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I must go now, my legs are tired.
Rest your feet. How did the baby sleep?
The baby is loud and small.
Little birds sing too. Do you have milk?
The drink is warm and good.
Warm things help bones. Is the door open?
Yes, the air is fresh.
Fresh air is kind. Do you need help?
No, I will be fine.
Goodbye then.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I want to clean my room but I feel stuck.
That is hard to do all at once. Do you have a small basket?
Yes, I have one right there.
Put one toy in it at a time. Can you pick up the shoes first?
I will try that now.
Good for you. How does it feel to start?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I am so scared of the big test today.
You can do this, I am sure you know the words. Do you like reading books?
Yes I do, but the math part looks hard.
Math is just counting things in a new way. Can you count to ten for me?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I feel lost in the time. What should I do?
Take a deep breath. Are you thinking of next week?
Maybe. But I do not know which month is coming.
That is a good start. Can you tell me the name of the month that just ended?
It was warm and sunny. I forget the name.
I do not know your season, so I cannot say. Do you know the first letter?
No. I just feel sad about the empty calendar.
Writing down three things to do helps. What is your first idea?
I want to clean my small room.
That is a strong and true plan.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to ride a bike in this busy city. How do I do it safely?
Look both ways before you cross any street. Do you know how to signal your turns?
Yes, I use my arm. What else should I watch for?
Keep your eyes on cars and people. Do you wear a helmet?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I found a pretty red flower by the pond.
That sounds lovely. Why is it red?
I think it is red because it is happy.
That is a sweet thought. Do you think it smells good?
It smells like sweet candy.
What a nice scent. Do you want to bring it home?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I ate toast with jam for breakfast. It was sweet and warm.
That sounds good. Do you like strawberry jam best?
Yes, I do. The sun was shining outside my window.
Nice. Did you see any birds today?
I saw a small blue one. It was very loud.
Birds can be loud. Did you give it a treat?
No, I did not have any food to share. I was in a hurry.
A fair excuse. Have a nice day.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I hate chess. I lost again and the board is so confusing.
That feels bad, I am sorry. Do you play for fun or to win?
Just to win, mostly. It feels like the computer cheats.
Computers do not cheat, but they play hard. Did you count your pieces?
I always lose my knights. It is so unfair.
Knights are tricky to guard. Do you check their safety first?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I counted the red dots ten times and still do not see nine.
That is a tricky part of counting. Do you like using your fingers to help?
I tried, but I forgot which dot I already touched.
Your fingers can get tired when we count fast. Would you like to try again, slowly?
Yes, please, I just need the right number to stay in my head.
We can count them one by one, very calm. Do you want to start with one?
Okay, one, two, three. My head feels very full.
Taking a small rest can help your brain. Are you ready to count the next few?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do we salt the meat before we cook it?
Salt makes it taste more like itself. Do you like salty food?
I wonder why the onions make my eyes hurt so much.
The smell is a sharp gas that wakes up your eyes. Are you crying a lot?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I saw a bright circle in the sky tonight. It looked like a ball of light hanging above the trees.
That is the moon. Did you feel calm watching it?
Yes, it made me feel quiet and happy. It was very far away but it still seemed to be watching me.
The moon stays with us all night. Do you plan to look at it again tomorrow?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I promised to help my friend, but I am very tired.
That feels hard. Do you have a small job you can do first?
I do not know what job is small enough.
I do not know your exact tasks, but ask if they need a quick hand.
I think I will try to do just one thing.
That is a good start.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to the park today. I saw a big dog chasing a ball.
That sounds like fun. Did you get to play with the dog too?
No, but I made a nice shape in the sand. It looked like a star.
A star in the sand is lovely. Do you want to write about that in your letter?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to the market today. I bought three big red apples.
Apples are good. What else did you see there?
I saw a nice dog sleeping near the vegetables. It looked very happy.
That is sweet. Do you like dogs?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why does the fish blow bubbles?
It is breathing. Do you like to watch them swim?
I do. Why is its tail moving so fast?
It needs to move the water. Is your tank warm?
Yes, it feels hot. Why do fish need warm water?
Cold water makes them sick. I do not know if yours is too hot.
That is scary. Why is it hiding behind the rock?
It feels safe there. Is the light on?
Yes, the light is bright. Why is it not eating?
It may be tired or sad. Do you want to turn the light off?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I dropped my ice cream today.
Oh no! That is very sad. Was it chocolate?
Yes, it hit the ground.
That feels messy. Do you have another one?
I bought a new one.
Good choice. I am happy for you.
It tastes the same.
That is good news. I do not know what color it is. Was it tasty?
Yes, I love it.
I am glad you are happy.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I bought some red roses today.
They look very nice. What color are they?
They are deep red.
Red is a happy color. Do you like them?
Yes, they make me smile.
That is great to hear. I am happy for you.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why does the moon look like a big ball?
It is a round rock in the sky. Do you like looking up at night?
The moon looks round sometimes.
That is called a full moon. Have you ever seen it low in the sky?
But sometimes it looks like a thin slice.
That is a crescent moon. Do you wonder why it changes shape?
What makes the moon change shape?
The Sun makes the light hit different parts. The moon stays the same shape all the time.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Is the light inside the lhouse spinning all day and night?
Yes, it shines to help ships see safe in the dark. Do you like watching boats?
I do, they look like toys from up here.
That is a sweet way to look at them. Is the sea calm today?
It is very calm, but the wind is cold.
The wind can be fierce near the tower. Do you wear a warm coat?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I feel lost on the sand. What should I do?
The water looks warm today. Do you like to swim?
I am scared of the waves.
That is a fair worry. Do you just want to sit and watch the sun?
Sitting sounds nice, but I want to play.
You can build a small fort with dry sand.
A fort sounds like fun. Can I do it?
Yes, you can. What shape do you want to make?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I forgot my math book.
Oh no, that is tricky. Did you bring your pencil?
Yes, but I do not know how to add big numbers.
We can start with small steps. What is two plus two?
Four. Can you help me with the rest?
I can help you try, yes. Is your book in your bag?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: My head hurts a lot.
That feels bad. Did you hit your head?
Yes, I fell on the ground.
I am sorry. I do not know much about falls.
It still hurts.
Maybe you need some rest. Do you want water?
Yes, please.
Here you go. I hope you feel better.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I am scared of the big pool.
It is okay to be scared. Do you like small pools better?
Yes, I do.
Good. Can you swim in the small pool?
I can kick my feet.
That is a good start.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: The ocean looks so big and deep. I am scared to swim in it.
It is a big place, but the water is kind if you stay close to the shore. Do you like playing in the sand?
Yes, I love sand. But what if a shark sees me?
Sharks do not like people, so they usually stay away. Do you have any friends coming with you?
My brother is with me. Should we go into the water now?
That sounds like a fun plan, but I do not know the weather there. Is it sunny and warm outside?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: My cat will not eat his food.
Is he playing with the toy more than eating?
Yes, he plays all day and then ignores the bowl.
Try moving the dish to a quiet spot.
That did not help. He still acts normal.
Has he peed or pooped recently?
Yes, he is using the box just fine.
If he stays well, give it one more day.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: I seem to be stuck in a loop. Why does that happen?
Maps can be confusing. Are you using a phone?
Yes, but the blue dot spins. Why does it spin?
I do not know for sure. Do you see a street sign?
There is a sign, but it is in another language. Why do signs change?
Cities have many words. Is the sign for a park?
It is just a wall. Why is there no way out?
Walls hide paths. Can you see a door?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to ride a bike, but I do not know which day to start.
You can start today, and I am glad to help. Which day feels best to you?
Saturday looks good because I have all day free.
Saturday is a great choice for practice. Do you have a helmet ready?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I stop my dog from barking?
Try giving him a treat when he stays quiet. Does he bark more at night?
Yes, he gets loud when I read books.
Try walking him extra long before bed to tire him out. Is he playing too much during the day?
He runs in the yard for an hour.
That is good, but he may need more brain games. Do you play hide and seek with him?
No, he only likes bones.
Try hiding small toys for him to find. Is he good at smelling things?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I just got back from a very long flight. It was so tiring but I am so happy to be here.
That sounds like a big trip. Do you have a favorite part?
Yes, the view of the clouds from the window was like a soft white blanket. It made me feel calm.
That must have been peaceful. Did you sleep?
I fell asleep for a while, but then I could not stop looking out the window. I was too excited to close my eyes.
I understand that feeling. Are you ready to rest now?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late. Where is the quiet street?
It is this way. Are you running for work?
Yes, I am running. Is it far from here?
It is not far. Do you like the quiet place?
I do not have time. Just point the way.
Go left. Is your bag heavy?
It is heavy. I must go now.
Take your time. Is it a good bag?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I am scared to ride the train.
That is a normal feeling. Do you like looking out the window?
Yes, I like to watch the trees go by.
The trip will be short and calm. Is your ticket ready?
Yes, I have it in my pocket.
Great, just stay near the seat. Are you eating a snack?
I have an apple with me.
That is a good choice. Have fun on your ride.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: How many months are in a year?
There are twelve months in one year. Do you know the names of them all?
I know January, but what comes next?
February comes right after January. It has the fewest days.
Is February short because it is the first month?
No, it is short by rule. Do you like the short month?
What month has the most days?
July has thirty-one days. It is a long month.
Do all months have the same length?
No, some have thirty days and some have thirty-one. I do not know which you like best.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: My legs feel very heavy on this long plane. Do they need to move?
Yes, your blood needs to move to stay safe. Do you have a glass of water with you?
Yes, I have a drink. How long until the plane lands?
I do not know the exact time. Are you getting hungry?
I am quite hungry. When do we get food on the trip?
Snacks usually come out before we land.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I have to run, but I feel so alone.
It is hard to feel left out. Do you have a friend nearby?
I am late, I cannot stay long.
I get it, time is tight. You are not alone right now.
Thanks, I need to go now.
I hope your day gets better. Tell me, what is your favorite food?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I feel lost. I do not know how to start learning a new talk.
That is okay. Do you like songs?
Yes, I love songs. But I am still stuck on what to pick.
Try singing along. You will learn words that way.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late. Did Rome have kings?
Yes, they did. Was that what you wanted to know?
No, wait. How long did those kings rule?
About two hundred and forty years. Do you like that story?
Almost there. Who was the first king?
His name was Romulus. Are you almost at your spot?
I am here now. Why did they drive the kings out?
The people wanted more freedom. I hope you have a good day.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I found a blue sock in my shoe.
That is lucky. Did you pack the other sock?
Yes, I put them in the bag. My bag is very heavy.
Oof, that sounds tough. Do you have a big lunch?
I packed an apple and a cracker. Now I must go.
Go with care. Have a happy day.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I just got off the train. It was so much fun.
That sounds like a great time. Did you see anything nice?
Yes, the hills were green and blue. The sun was shining too.
I am glad you had a nice view. How was the ride?
It was fast and smooth. I felt very lucky.
I am happy for you. Did you bring any food?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why did you promise me that?
I gave my word so you could feel safe. Do you trust me?
I think I do. Why is a promise so strong?
It binds my heart to my actions. Do you keep your promises?
I try very hard. Why do we break them sometimes?
Fear or haste can break a bond. I am sorry if I ever hurt you.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I found a dark tower by the sea. I do not know how to fix it.
It looks old and tired. Do you have a key?
I have a hammer, but I am scared to hit it.
A hammer might break the glass. Do you want to be a light keeper?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: My computer is not working.
Is the screen dark? Do you see any lights?
The light is off.
Please plug in the power cord. Is it tight?
It feels loose.
Push it in hard. Does the light turn on now?
It is on.
That is good news. What do you want to do next?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: My roses look sad and I do not know why.
That is a shame. Are the leaves dry?
Yes, they feel like paper. I think I killed them.
That feels bad, but you can try to save them. Did you give them water?
I watered them a lot, but the soil looks dry.
Dry soil needs more water than you think. What kind of pot are they in?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: My phone fell off the desk and hit the floor. The screen cracked but it still works.
Oh no, that must hurt. Did you break anything else?
No, just the phone. I am happy it still has my pictures.
That is good news. You are very careful today.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am so happy to tell you I am building a shed!
That sounds like a lot of fun. Do you have the wood ready?
Yes, I have all the wood and tools right here.
Good luck with the work. Is it a big shed?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: This line is so long. I am very tired.
I am sorry you are tired. Do you have a snack with you?
No, I do not. I just want to be done.
That feels hard. Is the place crowded today?
Yes, it is full of people.
That can take a long time. Do you like to play word games?
Maybe. I want to move now.
Moving helps your body. What game do you like to play?
Just let me go please.
I will help you wait.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am sad. The snow stopped falling.
That is tricky. Did you want to build a snowman?
Yes, but it is sunny now.
Sunlight is warm. Do you like warm days?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why is that box locked?
I do not know for sure. Is it big or small?
It is a big, heavy box.
It may hold old things from the past. Do you want to open it?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I feel very sad and I do not know what to do.
That feels bad. What is making you worry?
I just need to stop thinking so much.
It is okay to stop and breathe. Do you want to try a deep breath?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: Do you have any cookies?
Yes, we have warm cookies. Do you like chocolate chips?
I like the ones with raisins.
We have those too. Are they sticky?
Yes, they taste sweet.
Good, sweet is nice. Would you like a glass of milk?
Yes, please.
Here is your milk and cookies. Do you want to sit inside?
Yes, I do.
Great. Enjoy your snack.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am running late. What season is it?
It is winter. The trees are bare. Do you like the snow?
No time. I must go.
Okay. Be safe. Do you have a warm coat?
Yes. Bye.
Good luck. Have a good day.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: My chair leg is wobbling, and I do not know how to stop it.
That is a common problem. Is the loose leg on a hard floor or a soft rug?
It is on a hard floor, but it still moves.
Try tightening the screws first. If that fails, place a small piece of wood under the leg. Do you have any small wood pieces?
Yes, I have some wood shavings, but they look broken.
Wood shavings may work for now. They are not the best long-term fix, though. Can you reach the bolts?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why does the big hand move faster than the small hand?
The big hand goes around once for every hour, so it must race ahead. Do you like watching hands move?
Yes, I do. Why do we count twelve on the clock face?
That is just a very old way to split the day into equal parts. Do you ever watch the sun move?
Sometimes. Why is it dark when the hands are on twelve at night?
The earth spins away from the sun, so we see no light. Do you like the quiet of the night?
It is quiet. Why do we not just count the hours one to twenty-four?
I do not know for sure, but changing numbers every half day is harder to learn. Do you find twelve hard to say?
A little bit. Why do some clocks make a loud sound?
They wake us up when it is a new hour, so we do not sleep too late. Do you like being woken up?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I tried my best, but it did not work. I do not know what to do next.
It is okay to feel stuck. Do you want to take a small step again?
I am scared I will fail again. Should I just stop?
Failing helps you learn. What is one tiny thing you could try now?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: The lights went out. I do not know why.
That is scary. Did a big storm start?
No, it is quiet. But my breaker box is open.
Look inside. Do you see a switch in the middle?
Yes, one switch is down. Should I flip it?
Yes, push it up. Is it staying up?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to be a good friend to my new neighbor.
That is a nice thought. How do you usually talk to people?
I just say hello and wave.
Waving is a great start. Do you like to play outside?
I like to kick a ball around.
Kicking a ball is fun. Have you ever invited someone to play?
No, I am too shy to ask.
It is okay to feel shy. Try saying "Do you want to play?"
I will try that tomorrow.
I hope it works out.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: My sister has a new baby. What does he need?
He needs food, soft clothes, and a warm place to sleep. Are you excited to see him?
Yes, I am. How do I talk to him?
You can hum a song or sing softly. He likes quiet sounds.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am so happy. I love my big red apple.
That looks sweet. Do you like it cold?
Yes, it is very cold. I want to share one with you.
Thank you. Is it crunchy?
It is very crunchy and loud. It tastes like sugar.
I will take a bite. It is sweet and nice.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: My phone screen is cracked and I am so sad.
I am sorry to hear that. Do you have a way to fix it?
I do not know how to fix it.
That is tricky. Have you tried a backup?
I never made a backup.
I am not sure what to do then. Please be careful with the broken glass.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: My shirt has a big stain on it. What should I do?
Try to rub a little soap on it first. Do you have any soap?
Yes, I have some soap.
That is good. Put it in the cold water machine. Why did you not use hot water?
The tag says cold only.
You read the tag very well. That is a smart thing to do. Does it have a lot of little holes?
No, it is just big and white.
Great. Put it in the basket now. Do you like wearing that shirt?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I find a good book here?
Do you like stories or facts?
I like stories about animals.
Go to the shelf with blue labels.
Is that where the big books are?
Yes, and the small ones are next to them.
Thank you, I am going now.
Have fun reading.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I saw a big brown horse today. It looked very strong.
That sounds lovely. What did it look like?
It had a long, soft tail. I felt so happy just watching it.
I am glad you enjoyed the view. Did it smell like hay?
It smelled like sweet dirt. I want to see it again soon.
That is a great plan.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I feel very scared. What should I do?
That is a big feeling. Take a slow breath with me. What makes you feel this way?
I think I did a bad thing. I feel sad.
Sometimes we worry too much. Do you want to talk about it?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I really do not want to do my math homework. It feels too hard.
I am sorry it feels hard. What part makes you worry the most?
The word problems are so long and I get lost.
Taking small steps can help. Have you tried drawing a picture of the problem?
I guess I will try that now.
That sounds like a good plan.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I just built a new fence for my garden. It looks so nice.
That is great to hear. What color did you paint it?
I love how sunny and bright it feels. Thank you for asking.
You are welcome. Do you have flowers inside?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: What is a test?
A test checks what you know. Are you taking one today?
Yes, it is hard for me.
Do not worry. Can you read the questions?
Some of them are very long.
Take your time to read slow. Is the topic about math?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I went for a big walk today and I feel great.
That is wonderful to hear. How did your legs feel after?
My legs felt happy and strong, just like new ones.
That is a good sign that your body likes the move. Do you walk in the park?
Yes, I walk by the trees and see birds.
Nature makes a walk feel calm and fun.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I packed my bag for the trip. I found a lost glove from winter in the pocket.
That is a funny find. Did you keep the glove?
Yes, I put it back. It feels good to have my old things with me.
That sounds nice. Do you like winter?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: My boss is very kind. How do I fix a flat tire?
First, put the car on a flat spot. Do you have a tool kit?
Yes, I have the tools. What do I do next?
Use the jack to lift the car. Then take the old tire off.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I got one more card in my hand today.
That sounds like a small win. Did you win the round?
Yes, I did. The other cards did not help me.
Nice job. What did you play next?
I played a two. It was red.
Cool. Did you enjoy the game?
I did. Then I ate some pie.
Yum. Did you save any for later?
I did not. It was all gone.
That is fine. You worked up an appetite.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: My old friend called me today. I am so happy.
That sounds lovely. How did they seem?
They were very kind and told me about their new home.
I am glad they are doing well. Is the house near the sea?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why are clouds white sometimes?
Sunlight bounces off the tiny water drops. Do you like looking at the sky?
Yes, but why do they turn gray?
The drops grow big and thick, which blocks the light. I do not know why some storms get so loud.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: My fence is getting old and falling apart. What should I do?
Wood fences can rot, so you may need to replace the broken parts. Is the wood soft or just painted over?
It feels soft in some places. Should I fix it all?
You should replace any wood that feels squishy or dark. Do you like the current color of the fence?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: How do I catch a fish?
You need a rod and some bait. Do you have a rod?
I have a stick and a worm.
That will work well. Put the worm on the hook.
Where do I put the hook?
Put it in the water. Do you know where the fish swim?
I think near the rocks.
That is a good spot. Watch your line closely.
Why should I watch it?
Fish pull the line when they bite.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: The wind hit my window hard today.
That sounded scary. Did you close the blinds?
Yes, I shut them all. Then the rain started to pour down.
Wet clothes are not fun. Did you keep your shoes dry?
No, my shoes got very wet. But the sun came out just now.
Rain always leaves the sky bright. Do you like the quiet after the storm?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I broke my cup and feel very bad. What should I do?
You can buy a new one. Do you like red cups?
I do not have enough money. Is there a fix?
I do not know how to fix glass. Are you okay?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do bees make honey, and can I do it at home?
Bees collect sweet nectar and dry it out. Do you have a garden?
Yes, I have flowers in my yard.
You can pick the flowers to get the nectar. Have you tried eating flowers before?
No, I have not.
Many flowers are safe to eat. Just be sure to check which ones grow there.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I have no time for this mess.
I can help you fast. Is the floor the hardest part?
Yes, it is covered in dust.
Let us grab a broom together.
That sounds good, but I am rushing.
We will work quickly. Do you have a broom ready?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to plant seeds.
You can put them in small pots with good dirt. Do you have a sunny spot to put them?
I have a window box, but I do not know which seeds are good.
Try beans or sunflowers, as they grow fast. What color flowers do you like best?
I like yellow ones, but how do I know when to water them?
Check if the soil feels dry, and if so, give it a little water. I hope your plants grow tall and strong.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do the planes fly so high up?
They fly high to avoid bad weather. Do you see the clouds below?
I do. Why do my ears hurt?
The air pressure changes when the plane moves. It is a simple fix with gum.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I am lost in this big shop. I do not know where to go.
Do you want to buy a toy? I can help you find the fun section.
No, I want to eat a snack. But there are too many choices.
That is hard to pick. Do you like sweet things or salty things?
I like both, but I do not know which one to pick.
I do not know what you like best. Just pick the first one that looks good to you.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I take a photo on this phone?
Open the camera app and press the round button. Do you like taking pictures of food?
Yes, I love food photos. What if I want to save them?
They save all by themselves after you take the shot. Is your phone battery low?
No, it is full. How do I send a photo to a friend?
Tap the send icon in the corner and pick a friend. Do you know their number?
Yes, I do. That was easy.
I am glad you learned it. Let me know if you need more help.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I feel so quiet and sad here.
That sounds heavy. Do you have a stuffed animal to hug?
I do, but I do not want to play.
It is okay to rest. What is your favorite color when you are sad?
Blue, like the sky.
Blue is a nice color. Do you like to look out the window?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I want to clean my room. Where do I start?
Start with the floor. Do you have a vacuum?
I have a broom and a dustpan. How do I use them?
Sweep the dust toward the pan. Do you like a tidy floor?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am so happy today. Which day is it?
It is Monday. Do you like Mondays?
Yes, they are fresh and new.
That is a nice way to see it.
I love the weekend too.
Weekends are good for rest. What do you do then?
I sleep a lot.
That sounds nice and cozy.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I have a big meeting with my dad later today.
That sounds like a lot of grown-up talk. Are you excited to see him?
I am a little nervous because I have to tell him I broke a cup.
That is brave of you. Good luck telling him the truth.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do I need to level the ground first?
A flat base keeps your shed from tipping over. Do you have a level tool?
Yes, I found a level. Why is the wood usually pine?
Pine is light and easy to cut. Is it hard for you to lift?
No, I can lift it fine. Why do I need nails?
Nails hold the walls together tight. Do you have a hammer?
I have a hammer. Why should I paint the outside?
Paint stops the wood from rotting in the rain. I do not know your local weather.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I wanted to swim in the lake, but the water is too cold.
That sounds chilly. Do you have a warm coat?
No, I do not. I feel mad that I cannot swim.
I am sorry you feel that way.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to the park today. The sun was very warm. I saw a big red dog.
That sounds like a nice day. Did the dog have a treat?
Yes, it had a bone. It looked very happy. Then I went home to eat soup.
Soups can be very warm. What kind of soup did you have?
It was tomato soup. It was red and hot. Now I feel ready to make a plan.
That is a good step. Do you want to plan a walk for tomorrow?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: I want to learn to sing. Why should I do this?
Singing makes your heart feel good. Do you like happy songs?
I like them. Why does singing feel good?
It helps you breathe out your stress. Do you like to laugh?
Yes, I do. Is singing like laughing?
Yes, it lets you let go. Do you worry a lot?
Sometimes I do. Why does breath help?
Deep breaths calm your body. Do you feel calm after?
I think so. Why do people sing together?
It makes them feel close and safe. Do you have a group?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I have a big orange, but I do not know what to do.
Do you want to eat it or cut it?
I think I want to eat it, but I am not sure how.
That sounds good. Do you have a knife?
Yes, I have a knife, but I am scared to cut it.
Be careful with the sharp edge.
Can you tell me how to peel it?
I do not know the exact steps, but you can try to pull the skin off by hand.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I saw a red boat float down the river today.
That sounds like a nice view. Did the boat stop anywhere?
It stopped at a place with a small bridge.
Oh, a bridge sounds cool. Do you know what is under it?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I love singing in the mirror today.
That sounds fun. Do you sing happy songs?
Yes, I feel so light when I sing.
I am glad you are happy.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I found a bug on my leaf. Is it safe?
I am not sure what kind of bug it is. What color is it?
It is green and very small.
Green bugs are often harmless. Do they bite you?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I put a big block of wood in the water. Why does it not sink?
The wood pushes a lot of water aside. That push helps hold it up. Is your wood dry?
Yes, it is dry. But what makes a ship float if it is so heavy?
A ship is hollow, so it is light for its size. It pushes water up to stay high. Do you like boats?
Yes, I do. How do I make a toy boat that floats?
Use light things like cork or plastic. Shape it wide to push more water. Did you try that yet?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I did it! I finished my hard task.
That is wonderful news. What did you do?
I tried again and it worked.
I am so happy for you. Was it scary?
Not really, just a bit cold.
You did a great job.
I feel very warm inside now.
That is a nice feeling.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I feel sad today. Why?
Sadness is a normal feeling. Does your chest feel tight?
Yes, it does hurt a little.
That is your body telling you to stop and rest. Try taking three slow breaths. Do you like breathing games?
I do not know any.
I do not know your favorite, but you can count to ten. Do you want to try it now?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I want a pizza.
That sounds good. Do you like cheese on it?
Yes, please.
Great. Would you like a drink too?
Can I have juice?
Yes, that works. Do you want apple or orange?
Apple, please.
Okay, coming right up. Is this all you need?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I must go now. I promised to meet Sam at the park by noon.
That sounds like a good plan. Do you have all your things ready?
Yes, but I am very late. I will run to get there on time.
Running is a great way to go fast. Good luck with your promise.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I want a robot, but I do not know which one to get.
That is a big choice. What do you want your robot to do first?
I want it to talk, but I worry it will not know the right words.
Some robots learn new words fast. Do you like science stories?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do you throw the line so far?
I cast far to find where the fish are hiding. Do you like to sit by the water?
Why do you use a small worm?
A small worm looks like real food to a small fish. What color worm do you prefer?
Why is the lake so quiet?
It is quiet because the water is still and calm. Do you enjoy the peace?
Why did you not catch any fish?
I do not know why, as they are shy today.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: Is the new town quiet?
Yes, it is very quiet. Do you like quiet places?
Are there places to play?
I do not know for sure. Is that important to you?
Can I walk there safely?
Yes, the paths are safe.
