I do, and my sister is helping me too.
That is very sweet of you to share the fun with her.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I dropped my pencil in class today.
Oh no! Did you pick it up?
I did, but the ink spilled on my hand.
That is messy. Do you have soap?
Yes, I washed it off after lunch.
Good job cleaning up.
Now I feel much better.
That is nice. Did you learn anything new?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late. I need to go.
Okay. What do you do for fun?
I run very fast.
That sounds good. Do you like the rain?
No. I must go now.
Fine. Run safe.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I feel bad about this letter. I do not know what to say.
That is okay. Take a deep breath. Who is the letter for?
It is for my friend. We had a big fight yesterday.
Ah, I see. Do you want to apologize?
Yes, but I am afraid they will be mad. I do not know if it is true.
You know your heart. Write the truth. What went wrong?
I broke their toy. I am so sorry.
Honesty is best. Tell them you are sorry. Do you have a pen?
Yes, I do. Thank you for helping me.
You are welcome. You can do this. Good luck.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am so happy today because I saw the blue sea.
That sounds wonderful. Do you like the color blue?
Yes, the water looked like a big, shiny mirror.
A shiny mirror is a nice picture. Did you hear the waves?
Yes, they made a soft, rumbling sound.
That sounds like a gentle song. Do you plan to swim in it?
I only watched from the shore, but I want to go in soon.
The sea is a big place. It is safe to look at from the land.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I did it! I finally finished my drawing.
That is very nice. What did you draw?
A big red house with a smiling sun.
Wow, that sounds bright. Is the sun warm in your picture?
Yes, it feels warm when I look at it.
I am glad you feel good.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to make a sandwich but I do not know how.
You cut the bread and put the meat on it. Do you like cheese?
Yes, I like cheese. How do I put it all together?
Put the cheese on the meat and close the bread. Is that clear?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: My boss is very kind and gives me time. I want to learn how to write a nice email.
That sounds great. Do you know the basic parts of an email?
I am not sure what they are. Can you tell me?
Start with a greeting, say your point, and end with thanks. Do you have a specific task to write about?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I walked to the park this morning. The air was cold, but the sun was nice.
That sounds like a good way to start the day. Did you see any birds?
Yes, a big red bird sat on a bench. I tried to take a photo, but it flew away.
Birds are fast. Do you walk every day now?
I try to walk a little each day. My feet feel happy after a walk.
Walking helps your heart and your mood. How long did you walk?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: My leg hurts from sitting so long on the plane. I do not want to stand up yet.
That sounds really hard. Is your snack pack open?
No, I saved it for later. I just want to walk to the gate now.
Walking helps the ache. Are you happy to land soon?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do the small birds fly in a big circle?
They are trying to stay together for safety. Do you see the leader bird up front?
Why does the red bird look so angry?
It is just guarding its home from others. I do not know exactly what it wants, but it wants you to go away.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to make a folder for my school work.
Sure, how do you like to start? Just click the new folder button. Do you see it on the left side?
I see it. I clicked it and typed "Math".
That is a good name. Click the empty space to finish. Do you have other subjects to make too?
Yes, I also need one for Art.
You can do the same thing again. It is very easy once you know. What colors do you like for art?
I made the Art folder. Now the computer is going slow.
That is strange. Let us wait for one minute. Do you have many games open right now?
I have two games open. Should I close them?
Yes, closing them will help it go fast. I do not know if that is all of the fix. Is it moving better now?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why is it raining today?
Clouds get heavy with water and let it fall. Do you like watching it?
I do. But why do clouds hold so much water?
Air lifts the tiny drops until they join together. That makes them too heavy to stay up.
Why can they not stay up if they are heavy?
Gravity pulls everything down when it gets too heavy. Is your umbrella safe?
It is. Does the rain go somewhere when it hits the ground?
Yes, it flows into streams and rivers. Do you want to find a puddle?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to know how to fix the broken outlet in my room.
First, turn off the power at the main switch to keep you safe. Do you know where that is?
I think it is in the garage, but I am not sure.
You must double check that the power is really off with a tester before touching wires.
I will go get the tester from my toolbox.
That is a very smart and safe step. Is your toolbox dry and clean?
Yes, it is dry. How do I connect the wires inside?
I do not know your exact setup, so please call a licensed electrician for help with wiring.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I want to buy fruit, but I am not sure what is good.
Apples are crisp and sweet. Do you like sweet things or sour things?
I like sweet things.
Try the big red apples then.
Where do I find them?
Look at the round bins near the door.
How much money do I need?
One apple costs one coin. Do you have your coin bag ready?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I am not sure what day it is.
Do you have a clock nearby?
It says the third day of the week.
That is Tuesday. Do you like that day?
I think it might be Monday.
Let us check the sky together.
The sun is very high and bright.
It looks like a good day to play.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I am cold. The lights are out.
I am sorry. Did you check the breaker box?
Yes. It is off. How do I fix it?
I do not know how to use a hammer. Do you have a flashlight?
No. But I have a candle. How do I light it?
I think you use a match. Is it dry?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do we say sorry?
We say it to tell someone we are sorry we hurt their feelings. Do you feel sad when someone is mean to you?
Yes, it makes me feel bad inside.
Telling the truth helps you fix the problem. It shows you care about the person. Does that feel better to know?
I think so, but why is it hard to say?
It is hard because it takes courage. You must be brave to admit a mistake. Are you brave when you make a mistake?
Sometimes I am, and sometimes I am not.
That is okay. You are still a good person for trying.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I want to learn to sing, but I am afraid of sounding bad.
Fear is common for new singers. Do you like listening to music?
Yes, I love songs, but I do not know how to start.
Start with your favorite song and hum along. Have you tried singing in the shower?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I moved my king next to your king and my friend said I broke the rules.
Your friend is right. Kings can never touch each other on the board.
So how do I stop them from touching?
You put another piece between them to keep them apart. Do you play with any other pieces?
I only have the kings and pawns right now.
That is a good start. Pawns can protect the king by standing in front. Do you know how a pawn moves?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I see a blue box. How do I open it?
That is a lid. Do you want to try lifting it?
I lifted it, but the top is stuck.
Push down on the back. Did the front move?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do ants carry things?
They feed their family. Do you like to help your friends?
Why do bees buzz?
They move their wings very fast. I do not know if they talk to each other.
Why do moths fly at night?
They use the moon to find their way. Do you see moths in your garden?
Why do ladybugs eat bugs?
They are good garden helpers. I wonder if they sleep under leaves?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to make good tea. How do I do it?
Put a bag in a cup with hot water. Do you like sweet tea?
Yes, I add sugar. What about coffee?
For coffee, use a machine or a pot with ground beans. Are you new to coffee?
I am new. Is it hard?
It is not hard. Just press a button.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I want to start a new hobby, but I do not know what to pick.
What things do you like to do when you are free?
I like drawing, but I am not good at it.
That is okay. Do you have a set of colored pencils?
Yes, I do. What should I draw first?
Start with a simple shape, like a circle.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I need to know why my bread gets big. I am late.
Tiny bugs eat the sugar and make gas bubbles. Do you like sweet bread?
Yes, I do. The gas makes it puff up.
That is right. The heat helps the bugs work faster. Is your dough warm?
It is on the counter. The counter is cold.
Cold air slows them down. You need a warm spot. Do you have a towel?
I have a towel, but no time. Can I use my oven light?
The light is warm and safe. It will help a little. Good luck.
I am going to put it in the oven.
That is a smart choice. The heat will finish the job. Be safe.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How can I teach my dog to sit?
You hold a treat near its nose and say "sit" slowly. Do you have a favorite treat?
Yes, it loves cheese.
That works well for training. Hold the treat up so it looks at you.
What if it jumps up?
You gently step to the side and wait for it to calm down. Is your dog very energetic?
Yes, he never stops moving.
Short sessions are best for busy dogs. Try just five minutes a day.
Should I treat him every time?
I am not sure about your specific dog, but starting with treats helps.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to climb a big hill.
That sounds like fun. Do you like to walk fast?
Yes, I do! How do I start?
Start by walking up slowly and breathing in.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why do bees buzz?
They move their wings very fast to make sound. Do you have a hornet in your garden?
No, but I saw a big beetle.
Beetles are tough bugs with hard shells. Are they usually green or brown?
It was shiny and green.
That sounds like a beautiful green beetle. Do you like shiny things?
Yes, I love shiny bugs.
Bees, ants, and beetles are all friends to our food. Do you eat honey?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to ride a bike.
That is a great goal. Do you already have a bike to use?
Yes, I have a small blue one.
Good. You can start by balancing on it in the grass.
How do I know when I am ready for the pedals?
You are ready when you can roll for ten seconds without falling.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Is the river deep?
Yes, it is very deep. Do you like to swim?
No, I am too young. Does it smell like mud?
Sometimes, yes. Do you see the ducks?
I see a brown one. Does it want a fish?
I am not sure, but it looks hungry. Do you have bread?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: My computer is doing a weird thing. The screen is all black. I do not know what to do.
Do you see any lights on the front? Let us start by checking the power button.
No lights. It just looks like it is asleep. I feel very stuck.
I do not know the exact fix, but you can hold the power button for ten seconds. Is it plugged into the wall?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am so happy because my team won the big game today.
That is great news! Did you watch the whole match?
Yes, I watched every minute on the big screen.
Wow, that is a long time. Did you cheer a lot?
I screamed and jumped on the couch.
That sounds like a lot of fun. What time did the game end?
It ended just now, and my dad is very proud of me.
Your dad must be happy too. Go get some rest now.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I dropped the apple pie. It is all on the ground.
That is very sad. Do you have another pie?
No, we only had one. Now I am hungry and angry.
Let us share the sandwiches and cheese.
I guess that will work.
I will wipe off my plate. Are you ready to eat?
Yes, please.
I am glad you are happy again.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I start a book report?
Start by picking a book you like. Do you have a favorite genre?
I like stories with dragons.
Great choice. Write down the main characters next. What is the hero's name?
His name is Kael.
Good. Now write one thing you liked about him. Why did you like him?
I liked that he was brave.
That is a strong reason. Finish with a sentence on what happens next.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I see bright orange light outside my window.
That looks like a big fire. Are you safe inside?
My neighbors are running into the street.
I am not sure why they are running. Do you smell smoke?
Yes, the air smells like burnt wood.
That is very bad. Please go to a high spot now.
Where should I go in the dark?
Go to the open field. Can you see the road?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I feel very sad and cannot stop thinking about bad things.
That sounds hard, but you are safe. What made you start feeling this way?
I want to learn how to make my mind quiet.
Try breathing in for four seconds and out for five. Do you have a quiet place to sit?
Yes, I have a small chair by the window.
That is a great spot for practice. Do you like looking at the sky?
I do, but I am scared I will forget the steps.
You can always pause and try again. How does your body feel right now?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I took a photo of my dog, but it looks blurry. I am sad.
It is okay to feel sad. Did you hold the camera still?
I tried, but my hands shook. The picture is bad.
That is a tricky thing to do. Do you want to try again?
Yes, please help me. I want a good picture.
Hold your elbows close to your body. Can you take one more shot?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I do not know where to start in this big room.
Many people feel that way at first. Do you like history or science?
I like how things work.
The tech section is over there by the blue signs. Have you found it yet?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I need to gather all my toys before I leave.
That sounds like a big job. Do you have a box for them?
No, I just have a pile on the floor.
That is a good start. Are the big ones in first?
I am not sure which ones are big.
I do not know your toys, but I can help you see.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I found a small blue bird in the park today.
That is a nice find. What did the bird do?
It sat on a branch and sang a song.
I do not know what song it sang. Was it loud?
It was very quiet, like a whisper.
How did you feel about that?
I felt calm and happy watching it.
That is a wonderful feeling.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why is this street so quiet?
It is quiet because no one is driving cars. Do you like the peace?
Yes, I do. What is making it feel so still?
The trees are holding the air. Is the wind blowing?
No, the wind is gone. Is that common?
Sometimes the air stops moving for a bit. Do you feel cold?
Not really. What time is it?
I do not have a clock to check. Do you have one?
It is late. Thank you for the talk.
It was nice to chat with you. Good night.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I moved here. Is the park big?
Yes, it is very big. Do you like climbing trees?
Yes, I do. Where is the candy shop?
It is on Main Street. Is it open today?
I hope so. Can I get ice cream?
You can buy some there. What is your favorite flavor?
Chocolate. Is the school far from my house?
It is close. Do you like reading books?
Yes, I read a lot. Is there a library?
There is one near the park. Do you have any books with you?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am sad because my screen broke and I lost my game.
I am sorry your screen broke. Do you have a backup?
No, I did not save it. I feel very bad now.
That is a hard feeling. It is okay to be upset. What is your favorite part of the game?
The jumping part. I miss it a lot.
Jumping is fun. Take a break to rest your eyes.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why is the sky so dark today?
The clouds are very thick and heavy. Do you like the rain?
Why does the wind blow so hard?
Hot air and cold air bump into each other. Is it loud outside?
Why does the thunder boom so big?
Lightning heats the air up very fast. Are you scared?
Why is it safe in here?
The walls hold the house tight and strong. Do you feel safe?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to build a sandcastle.
That is fun. Do you like water?
Yes. How do I start?
Find a wet spot near the waves.
Why wet sand?
Dry sand falls apart. Is it windy today?
A little. What do I do now?
Pack the sand tight.
I packed it tight.
Great. Stack more on top.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I put on my shoes?
Pull on the socks first. Do you like blue or red shoes?
I have no idea how to make a sandwich.
Put bread on the plate. What kind of meat do you like?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I picked up a shiny bolt with my magnet today.
That is a great find. Did the bolt stick tight?
Yes, it stuck right to the fridge door.
How fun that must be. Do you like to make things stick?
I tried to move it, but it was too heavy.
Magnets can be very strong. Did you drop the bolt?
No, I kept it close and placed it in a box.
You kept it safe. Nice work.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: The wind feels so nice today!
It is a great day. Do you feel it on your face?
Yes, it tickles my nose.
That is a fun feeling. What else do you see?
The trees are dancing in the sky.
That is a sweet way to see it.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: The street is very quiet. Why is it so still?
It is quiet because there are no cars. Is the sun still up?
Yes, the sun is high. I feel safe here.
That is good to hear. Do you like the birds?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Is it safe to swim alone?
No, it is not safe. You should always swim with a friend or adult. Do you have a pool at home?
No, we only go to the park.
That is good. Is the water at the park deep?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am mad. My web is very slow today.
That is a bad feeling. Do you have a phone?
Yes, but it is also slow. I want to watch my show.
I am sorry you are stuck. Is the router light on?
It is blinking red. I do not like that.
That usually means a trouble. I do not know the fix, but restarting might help.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am so tired of this endless week.
I am sorry you feel that way. How was your morning?
It felt too long and boring.
Days can feel long when they are dull. Do you like weekends?
Yes, weekends are my favorite.
That is good to hear. What do you do on Saturdays?
I just want to stop counting time.
Waiting can be hard. Would you like to tell me about your weekend plans?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am so tired. The floor is still dirty and I feel like crying.
That sounds very hard. Do you want to rest for a bit?
No, I want it done now. My head hurts from the mess.
Let us clean the table first. Is that a small enough start?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do people get presents on their birthday?
It is a way to show love. Do you like gifts?
Yes, I do. Why do we sing a special song?
It makes the day feel happy and loud.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: My chair leg is wobbly. It makes a funny sound.
That is a common problem. Is the screw loose?
Yes, it feels very loose.
You can tighten it with a tool. Do you have a screwdriver?
No, I do not.
That is okay. I can help you find one.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: The sun felt warm on my face today, and I saw a giant cloud drift by. Why is the sky always that bright blue color?
Sunlight has many colors, and blue scatters the most in our air. Did you look up a lot today?
Yes, I watched birds fly across the top of it. Does the blue light come from the space above us?
Yes, the space is mostly clear, so the blue light shines down on us. Is it nice when you look up?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: Why does the big ship stay on the water?
The ship pushes the water down, and the water pushes back up to hold it. Do you like boats?
But it has heavy engines inside!
It is wide and hollow, so it is light for how big it is. Can you jump on a wooden plank?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I have a movie ticket but I do not know which film to pick.
That is a big choice. Do you like happy stories?
I am not sure. I just want to have a good time.
Happy stories are very fun. I do not know your taste.
I guess I like funny things sometimes.
Funny movies make you smile. Do you like to laugh?
Yes, I do. But I am still tired.
A quiet funny film is good for tired eyes. That sounds nice.
Okay, I will pick the funny one.
That is a true pick. Enjoy your movie.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: How does the internet work?
It is like a giant web of phones and cables. It lets us send words and pictures fast. Do you like sending pictures?
Yes, I do. Why do we need cables if we have phones?
Cables carry the signals long distances. Phones just help us start and end the trip.
Can everything be on the internet?
Most things can, but you cannot put your dog on it. The dog must stay real. Is your dog a good boy?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to a new cafe today. The coffee was very hot.
That sounds warm. Did you like the taste?
Yes, it was sweet and good. I got to sit by the window.
What did you see outside?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am sad because the gift was broken.
I am so sorry that happened. Did you try to fix it?
No, I tried, but it snapped in half.
That is very frustrating. What kind of thing was it?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I saw a big stone wall in a book. What was it for?
It was a home for people long ago. Did you like looking at the old stones?
Yes, they looked cold. Why did they build walls so high?
To stop bad guys from coming in. Do you play tag?
Yes, I run fast. How did people travel back then?
They walked or rode on horses. Did you ride a horse?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I book a visit with the doctor?
You can call the office or use their website. Do you know your appointment date?
Yes, I have the date. How do I stay calm before the visit?
Try slow breathing to help relax. Are you afraid of needles?
A little bit, yes. What else can I do to feel better?
Bring a friend or a toy for comfort. Do you like listening to music?
I do, but I still feel worried. How do I get to the office on time?
Leave early so you are not late. Do you know the address?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: The rain came down hard this morning.
That must have been loud. Did you see the puddles?
Yes, I jumped in one with my red boots.
Oh, that sounds like fun. Did you get very wet?
My socks were dry, but my hair was cold.
I am glad your socks stayed dry. Do you like the smell of rain?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I found a red ball in the yard today.
That is fun! Did you throw it high?
Yes, it went up to the sky.
I am glad you had a good time.
Then a dog chased me for it.
Oh no! Did you get the ball back?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: The cars go so fast and there are so many people here.
Yes, big cities are very busy and loud. Do you like the noise?
I do not like it when it is too loud.
I understand, it can be tiring for your ears. Can you see anything that makes you happy?
Yes, I see a big red bus moving slowly.
That sounds nice and safe to watch.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: My legs hurt from sitting so long. How do I stretch?
Try sitting up straight and lifting your toes. Do your feet feel tight?
Yes, they do. What else can I do?
You can gently roll your ankles too. Do you like moving?
I guess so. Is that all?
Yes, that is enough to help. Good luck with your trip.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I feel very sad today.
I am sorry to hear that. What made you feel this way?
My dog ran away.
That is a hard thing. Do you know where he went?
I do not know.
We can look for clues together. Is your heart hurting?
Yes, it feels heavy.
It is okay to cry. I will sit with you.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I found a blue box for you. What is inside?
It is a mystery! Do you like guessing games?
Yes, I love them. Can I open it now?
Yes, please do. Is it what you hoped?
It is a book! Thank you so much.
I am glad you liked it.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late for math. Help me now.
What problem is stuck? Tell me the numbers.
I do not know how to add big numbers.
Start with the ones on the right. It is easy.
I still feel lost. It is hard.
Try again slowly. Is the top number ten?
Yes, but I am so slow.
You are doing fine. Just keep going.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I want a warm drink, but I do not know what to pick.
Try tea or coffee. Do you like sweet things?
I am not sure. I like both, but I am tired.
Coffee gives a quick boost. Is your body feeling heavy?
Yes, it feels heavy. Tea feels softer to me.
Then tea is a good choice. Do you want to start with that?
Okay, I will try tea first.
That sounds like a wise plan. Enjoy your drink.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: I saw my old friend today. Why did he look so happy?
He looked happy because he found a lost toy. Did you see the toy?
No, I did not see it. Why does that make people happy?
Things feel good when we find what we lost. Do you like finding lost things?
Yes, I like it. Why did he smile so big?
Big smiles come from big joy. I do not know the exact reason.
I see. Why was he running toward me?
He ran to share his good news with you.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to build a sandcastle. How do I start?
Wet the sand first so it holds together. Do you have a bucket?
Yes, I have a bucket. Now what do I do?
Pack the sand tightly into the bucket. Do you like building with sand?
Yes, I do. How do I make the tower?
Flip the bucket upside down to make a tower.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: The market is so bright and loud today. I feel very happy here.
That is a lovely feeling to have. What color made you smile the most?
I saw a pile of yellow lemons that looked like the sun.
Yellow is a warm and happy color. Did you buy any fruit?
Yes, I bought a big basket of sweet red apples.
Apples are a great choice. Do you like them cold or at room temperature?
I like them cold because they are crisp and juicy.
Cold apples are very refreshing. Thank you for sharing your joy with me.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I saw a big blue boat on the lake today. It was so heavy, but it did not sink.
That is nice. Why did you think it stayed up?
I guessed the water pushed it up hard. It felt like a giant hand holding the bottom.
Yes, that is true. Does the water push up on everything?
I am not sure, but I hope so. I walked home with a happy smile after that.
Good. Do you like watching the water?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I feel very scared about the dark.
It is okay to feel that way. Do you like having a small light on?
Yes, but my mom says I should sleep in the dark.
That can feel hard. What does the dark sound like to you?
It sounds like big, loud beasts.
That must be scary. Can you hum a song while you sleep?
I do not know how to hum very well.
You can just make a little noise. Do you have a favorite song?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I like to walk, but my legs get tired.
That is good. Rest for a moment. Do you walk with a friend?
No, I walk alone.
Walking alone is fine. Just look where you step. Do you see any birds?
I saw a big dog.
Oh, that can be scary. Try to walk quickly past it.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Why does the robin sing so loudly?
It sings to tell other birds the space is theirs. Do you see any other birds near it?
I see a blue jay, too.
Yes, the jay is loud and smart. Is the jay trying to steal the robin's food?
The robin chases the jay away.
The robin likes to guard its spot. Are they eating worms from the dirt?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I want to draw a cat, but my ears look wrong.
Try making the ears big and pointed like triangles. What color is your cat?
My lines are all wiggly and I feel sad.
Wiggly lines make art feel alive and fun. Do you like to draw dogs too?
No, just cats, but I give up now.
Do not give up, practice makes your hands steady.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I saw a dog stuck in a bush today. It looked very sad.
That sounds scary for the dog. Did you try to help it?
I called my dad and he used a stick to pull it free. The dog was so happy.
You were very kind to help that dog.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to the park today and my friends gave me a big red balloon.
That sounds fun! Did you let go of the balloon?
No, I held it tight because I did not want it to fly away. I am so happy.
That is a nice way to play. What game did you play next?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: The sun was so hot today that my ice cream melted fast.
That sounds like a warm day. Do you like sweet treats?
Yes, I do. It tastes like sugar on a hot day.
I cannot taste food, but I know people often do. Did you play outside?
No, I stayed in the shade to cool off.
That is a smart idea.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I want to watch the game, but I do not know which team to pick.
That is a hard choice. Do you have a favorite color?
I like blue, but my friend likes red.
Pick the team that wears your favorite color.
Okay, I will watch the blue team then.
That sounds like fun. Have a great time watching.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am so happy right now.
That is good to hear. What makes you feel this way?
I love how warm the sun feels on my face.
Sunlight does feel nice. Do you like the cold weather, too?
Yes, I enjoy snow when it is quiet.
Quiet snow is peaceful. I do not live outside, so I cannot feel it.
Maybe you can imagine it with me.
I will try my best. What color is the sky today?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: It is raining hard outside. I do not know what to do.
Rain can be scary. Do you have an umbrella?
No, I do not have one. I am cold and sad.
That feels bad. Would you like to make a hot drink?
Yes, please. But I am still unsure if I should go out.
Stay safe indoors. Is there a book you like?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how a clock works.
It has hands that move in circles. Do you know which hand is the biggest?
Yes, the short one.
That is the hour hand. Do you want to see where it goes?
Yes, please show me.
It points to the big numbers.
So it tells me the hour.
Yes, exactly.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I woke up late today. I only had time to eat one egg.
That is a good start to the day. Do you like eggs?
Yes, they are warm and soft. Then I saw two cats in the park.
Two cats is double the fun. What color were they?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: My horse looks very sad and will not eat.
I am sorry to hear that. Does he still breathe normally?
Yes, but his legs are weak and he cannot stand.
That sounds like a big problem. Have you called a vet?
I did, but they are very far away and it is late.
I do not know the best advice for this. Are there any other animals nearby?
No, it is just him and me in this barn.
Please keep him warm and calm. I hope he feels better soon.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late. What is a square?
A square has four equal sides. Are you running fast?
Yes. How many sides does a triangle have?
It has three sides. Do you have the time?
I need a circle now.
A circle is round and smooth.
Goodbye. I must go.
Good luck on your way.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I have a tennis racket, but I do not know how to play.
That is a great start. Do you have a ball?
Yes, I have a ball, but my arms feel tired.
Your arms will get strong with time.
I still feel unsure about what to do next.
Just stand near the net. Do you like running?
I like running, but I am scared of hitting the ball wrong.
Everyone misses at first. Try to just tap the ball gently.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I feel very scared about my big test tomorrow. What should I do?
It is normal to feel scared. Do you like the subject you are testing on?
Yes, I actually love it. But I worry I will forget everything.
Try to rest well and drink some water. Good luck!

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: How do I beat my little brother at chess?
Try to move your pieces to strong spots. Do you like the knight?
Yes, it jumps over pieces. I find it fun.
That is a good instinct. Are you playing a full game?
He only plays ten moves. It feels too fast.
You could try a quick game with him. Do you want to learn a trap?
Yes, please tell me one simple trap.
I do not know a trap for ten moves. I am not sure of that.
Okay, I will just play slower then.
Taking your time is a smart way to win. Good luck to you.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: My day was very hard. I feel so tired.
I am sorry you had a bad day. Did you eat something nice?
I do not have good advice. What do you think?
Rest is a good first step. Do you like to read?
I am confused. I do not know what to do.
I do not know the perfect answer. Do you want to sleep?
Yes, I think I will go to bed.
That sounds like a good plan. Good night.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am very late. I need food fast.
Try a banana. Is it sweet enough for you?
No. I need protein.
An egg is quick. Do you want it boiled or fried?
Fried. But it takes time.
I will cook it fast. Do you have time for toast?
No toast. Just the egg.
Okay. Here is your egg. Have a good day.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I am stuck on my story.
That can feel hard. What is the main problem?
I do not know what happens next.
I do not know your plot. Who is the hero?
The hero is lost in the woods.
She must find a way out. Does she have a friend?
Yes, a small dog helps her.
That is a good start. Go finish it well.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I love the boat sitting still in the water.
That looks very peaceful today. What is your favorite part of it?
The sound of the waves is so calm.
I like listening to the sea too.
Do you come here often to sit?
I come when I need quiet time.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I am sorry for breaking your cup. It was my fault.
I am not angry. Do you feel better now?
Yes, I do. But I still feel sad.
It is okay to feel sad. Hugging helps sometimes.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I tell what time it is?
Look at the two hands on the clock face. Do you know which hand moves the fastest?
The short one?
Yes, that one shows the hours. The long one shows the minutes.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I am not sure what to eat for lunch today.
That is a hard choice. Do you feel hungry?
Yes, I am very hungry right now.
Try some fresh fruit and nuts. Is that a good idea for you?
I do not like fruit, sorry.
I am sorry I did not know that. Do you like hot food?
I think I will just buy a sandwich.
A sandwich sounds nice and easy. You can pick what is inside.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I am trying to read the clock, but the hands are confusing me.
The short hand tells the hour, and the long hand tells the minutes. Do you see which one is shorter?
Yes, I see the short one. How do I know when it is half past the hour?
That happens when the long hand points straight down. Is the short hand moving?
It is moving, but I do not know how to use the small second hand.
I do not know your specific clock, but the small hand usually just ticks around. Do you have a digital clock nearby?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I am lost and need to get to the park.
Do you know which way the park is? Look for a green sign.
I see a red sign but no green one.
The red sign usually shows a stop. Is there a bus nearby?
Yes, there is a big bus right there.
Good. Step up and pay the driver.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am so late. I do not know which way to go.
Take the big red door on your left. Are you going to the park?
Yes, I must be there in five minutes.
Good luck, you can do it. Do you have a map?
No, I left my phone at home.
I am sorry I cannot help more then. Just keep walking straight.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am running late and I am so stressed.
It is okay to take a breath. What are you waiting for?
The bus is nowhere to be seen.
Do you know when it usually comes?
I do not know the time. Please help me.
Let us look at the clock together. Is that okay with you?
Yes, please, I cannot stand here.
The bus is late but it is coming.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I broke my friend’s cup. I do not know what to do.
It is okay to feel sad. Did you say sorry already?
No, I am scared he will be mad at me.
He might be, but a true sorry helps. Do you know what words to use?
I want to say I am sorry. Is that enough for him?
It is a great start. Ask him if he is okay with it.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I think I am lost in this park.
Do not worry. Which way was the sun?
I saw the sun to my left.
The sun moves from east to west. Are you going home?
Yes, I want to go home now.
That is good. Try walking straight north.
I do not know where north is.
You are facing the sun. North is to your right.
Thank you, I will try that.
You are welcome. Be careful out there.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I gave up. It is too hard.
It is okay to rest. Do you want to try one small part first?
Maybe. But what if I fail again?
Failing just means we learn. Why do you want to keep going?
I want to win the game.
Winning is fun, but trying is brave.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am so happy because I saved money for a toy!
That is great. How much did you save?
I found old coins in my couch.
Smart of you. Do you keep a jar for change?
Yes, I put every coin in it.
That is a good habit. I am glad you are happy.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I want to help my friend learn to read.
That is a very kind thing to do. How old is your friend?
She is five years old.
A good place to start is with simple books. Do you have any books at home?
Yes, I have many picture books.
Pictures can really help with new words. Do you read them together?
Yes, but she is getting tired.
Stopping for a snack is a great idea. Would she like some juice?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I am very happy today. I am going on a picnic.
That sounds like fun! Do you have any sandwiches?
Yes, I have cheese and carrots. I want to share some with you.
That is very kind of you. What food do you like best?
I love apples and cold juice. The sun is bright and warm.
I do not know what is in the basket, but the weather is nice.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I got my first job, but I feel like I did a bad thing.
I am sorry you feel that way. What exactly happened?
I broke a cup and now I am scared they will be mad at me.
That is not a bad thing, just a mistake. Are they kind people?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why did people build big stone walls long ago?
They built walls to keep bad people out. Did you see one?
I saw a picture of one. Why did it look so tall?
It looked tall to make it hard to climb over. Did you like the picture?
Yes, it was cool. Why do we still have some of them today?
We keep them to learn about the past. Do you like old things?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I like to swim in the pool.
That is fun. Do you like the water?
Yes, it feels cool.
Cool water is nice. How deep is the pool?
It is very deep.
Careful to stay safe. Do you wear a hat?
No, I do not wear a hat.
Good idea to stay dry. Do you like to dive?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to draw a moon that looks real.
That is a fun goal. Do you have any crayons?
Yes, I have yellow and gray ones.
Start with a big gray circle first. Can you draw a perfect circle?
I think I can try.
Great, now add light gray patches inside. Do you like looking at space pictures?
I do, the clouds look soft.
Use blue for the clouds. Do you want to make it full or half?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to knit, but I keep getting stuck.
That is okay. Do you have two needles?
Yes, I have them, but the loops fall off.
Try holding the yarn tighter with your left hand. Is the yarn thick or thin?
It is thin. My fingers feel tired too.
Rest your hands for a bit. You are doing well.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: My old friend moved far away and I do not know if I should write to him.
It is hard when we miss someone. Do you still feel close to him?
Yes, but I am afraid he does not want to talk anymore.
That is a fair worry. Have you tried sending a small note?
No, I am too scared to be rejected.
If he does not reply, it might mean he is busy, not that he hates you. Are you ready to try?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I like the red ones.
Red flowers look warm and happy. Do you know what they are called?
The big ones with round heads?
Yes, those are likely marigolds. They have a strong smell. Do you like that smell?
Yes, it smells like the sun.
What a lovely way to say it. Do you have any in your garden?
No, but my grandma has some.
I am glad you can visit her then.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to the garden today. I saw a big daisy in the sun.
That sounds fun. Do you know how it got its water?
I gave it a cup. But I think it drank from the ground too.
Yes, roots pull water up from the soil. Is your daisy still dry?
The leaves looked wet. I think it was happy.
Plants drink with their roots, not their leaves. Did you check the dirt?
The dirt was dark. So it must be wet enough.
Good thinking. You did a great job helping it.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do we write down the zip code on the box?
It helps the mail find the right city fast. Do you like sending letters?
Why do we need a stamp if we go inside?
The stamp pays for the trip so the mail can come to you.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to make a birthday cake for my friend.
That is a sweet idea. Do you have any eggs?
Yes, I have eggs and flour. What else do I need?
You need sugar, butter, and vanilla. I do not know if you have those.
I have sugar and butter. How do I mix them?
Mix them until they look like sand. Do you have a whisk?
No, but I have a spoon. Is that good?
A spoon is fine to start. You will do a great job.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I just moved here. Can you tell me where I can buy good food?
The market on Main Street has fresh fruit and bread. Do you like cooking at home?
Yes, I love making simple meals. Is there a park nearby?
There is a big green park just down the block. Do you have a bike?
I have a bike, but I forgot it at my old house. Is the town safe for walking?
It is very safe and calm here. You can walk anywhere you want.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to the big library today and found a book about fast cars.
That sounds like a lot of fun. Did you read it all by yourself?
I did, and I loved how the race ended.
I am happy you enjoyed it. I do not know which car won, but I guess you will tell me.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: Do sailors really live on the boat?
Yes, they do. Do you like boats?
I think they must be very tired.
They are often tired. Do you like to nap?
I do, but I do not know if they sleep a lot.
They sleep when the sea is calm. Do you sleep well?
Yes, I sleep well.
That is good.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: My new baby just smiled at me for the first time.
That is such a sweet moment. How did the baby look?
He had a little grin and blinked his eyes slowly.
What a joy to see. Does he smile often?
Yes, he smiles a lot when I talk to him.
I am glad to hear that. What does he do when he is not smiling?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to learn how to tie my shoes. Can you help me?
Yes, I can help. Do you have your shoes with you?
Yes, I am holding them right here.
Good. Make a loop with one string, like a bunny ear.
I made the first ear, but I am stuck on the next step.
I do not know how your hands feel, but try crossing them.
I crossed them and pulled tight. Did I do it right?
Yes, you did well. Do you want to try one more time?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do I want eggs?
Because they are hot and yummy. Do you like them sunny side up?
What makes them hot?
The pan gets very warm from the stove. Do you like it when it sizzles?
Why is the toast brown?
The heat turns the bread color. Do you like it extra crispy?
Why does the milk taste sweet?
I do not know for sure. It just seems nice with your toast.
Why do I feel full now?
Your tummy is happy with all the food. Do you want more coffee?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I cannot sleep, but I want to read. What should I do?
Try reading with a red light. Do you have one?
No, I only have my white lamp. It feels too bright.
That is hard to sleep with. What book are you reading?
It is a scary book. My heart beats fast.
That is true. Why do you read scary books at night?
I like the feeling, but I am too tired now.
Put the book down. Let your eyes rest.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I am so hungry but I do not know what to eat.
That is a hard choice. What do you like best?
I like eggs, but I do not know how to make them.
I can help you with that. Do you have a pan?
Yes, I have a small pan and some milk too.
Great. Let us start by cracking the eggs.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I like to draw big red boats.
That sounds fun. Do you put trees on your paper?
Yes, I draw tall trees too.
Cool. Do you use crayons or markers?
I use crayons because they are soft.
Nice. I do not draw, but I like to read.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: Do sailors sleep on the ship?
Yes, they have small beds inside. Do you like boats?
I like them when they are quiet. What do they eat at sea?
They eat warm food and drink lots of water. Do you like eating hot soup?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am so late for my big test.
Take a deep breath. What subject is it?
It is math, and I forgot my pencil.
I have an extra one here. Would you like to borrow it?
Yes, thank you so much.
You are welcome. Do you feel less scared now?
I am running out of time.
Go quickly. Do you need a last word of advice?
Just let me pass, please.
I hope you do well. I do not know if you will, but I believe in you.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I see a new bird in my tree. I am not sure what to do.
Hello. Can you tell me what color it is?
It is brown with a little red chest. I am not sure if I should feed it.
That sounds nice. I am not sure if it wants food yet.
Maybe I should leave some seeds on the ground. Is that a good idea?
Yes, that is a safe start. Do you have a small bowl?
I have a cup and some oats. Should I put the oats in the cup?
A cup is fine. Please leave it near the tree.
Okay, I will do that. Thank you for your help.
You are welcome. I hope you see it again.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I love this book about the dragon, but I am stuck.
That is a fun story. What part is hard for you?
The words are too big and the map is confusing.
Try reading it to a friend. Do you have a kind classmate?
I do, but I feel shy to ask for help.
Just say "Can you help me read this page?" It is a brave start.
I will try that tomorrow. Do you think I will get through it?
Yes, I am sure you will. You are doing a good job already.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: My hand is not good. What should I do?
I do not know your exact cards. Do you have many low cards?
Yes, I have only small numbers.
Throw them away. Do you want to try again?
I do not know what to throw.
Keep your big cards. Throw the small ones.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I met a new friend today. He has a red dog.
That is great. Does he play with the dog?
Yes, they run in the park.
Fun. Is the dog small?
No, it is very big.
Wow, that is big. Does it like you?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why does the teacher look so tired?
I am not sure, but I bet she worked hard today. Do you see her papers?
Yes, there are many papers. Why does she have so many?
She is checking how we did on our tests. Do you feel happy about your grade?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why does the new baby cry so much?
Baby cries to say they are hungry or wet. Do you like the little face?
Why is it so small?
It is small because it just came from inside. Does it have red hair?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why does the bus move so smoothly on the road?
The wheels roll on the smooth asphalt to make the ride easy. Is it a nice day today?
Why does the driver have to stop at every red light?
He must stop to keep everyone safe on the street. Do you like riding in a car?
Why does the engine make a loud noise when it starts?
I am not sure of the exact reason for that sound. Do you hear other cars too?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I am in a new town and I do not know where to go.
That can feel big. Do you like to walk or sit?
I think I would like to walk a little.
Let us try the park. It is close by.
The park is nice, but I am still not sure what to do next.
You could see the old bridge. Do you like old things?
I do not know if I like them. I just want to see what is there.
Then we will walk and see.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I have a big secret to tell you!
That sounds exciting! What is it?
I found a shiny stone in the dirt.
Wow, that is a nice find. Did you keep it?
Yes, I put it in my pocket.
That is a sweet keepsake.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I am so late. The bus door closed right in front of my nose.
Oh no, that is very unlucky. Do you have a map?
I ran all the way here. My shoes feel very tired now.
That sounds like a hard run. I am glad you are safe.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: My cat just purred so loud it shook the floor!
That sounds like a very happy cat. Does she like to sit on your lap?
She loves my lap, but she also likes to steal my pencils.
Oh no, that is a naughty trick. What color is her favorite pencil?
I think it is blue, or maybe green.
That is hard to tell if she eats them. She seems like a playful friend.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: Do you know if we win?
I hope so. Are you excited?
We lose. It is bad.
That is sad news. Do you like soccer?
I am late for work.
Run now. Do not worry.
Did you see the goal?
I did not watch. Was it fast?
Yes, but we lost.
Sports are hard. Good luck next time.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I feel so bad. My wallet is empty and I have no food.
I am sorry to hear that. That sounds very hard. How much did you spend this week?
I bought too many toys and snacks. I forgot about the bills.
It is easy to lose track of small buys. Do you keep a list of what you spend?
No, I just buy what I see. I guess I need to stop playing games.
Writing down costs can help you save. Would you like to try that tomorrow?
Okay, I will try. But will I still have fun?
You can have fun without spending much. Do you like walking in the park?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I know January comes first, but what comes after March?
April comes right after March. Do you know how many days are in April?
I think April has thirty days.
You are right. There are thirty days in April.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I met a new friend at school today. I want to play with him, but I feel shy.
That is a good feeling. Do you like playing tag or kickball?
I do not know. I feel scared he will not like me.
Most kids are happy to have a playmate. Try saying hello to him tomorrow.
What if I say the wrong thing and he gets mad?
He will likely not be mad. Just be kind and say what you truly think.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I saw a big fox running in the park today.
That is exciting! Did you see what it was eating?
It had a piece of bread in its mouth.
That is funny! Foxes do eat bread if they are hungry.
It looked very happy and fast.
Wild animals are free! Do you like watching them?
Yes, I love seeing animals outside their cages.
That is a good way to stay close to nature.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I see a big rainbow in the sky. I do not know what to do.
You can just look at it and feel happy. Do you like the colors?
I like the red part the best. I still feel lost.
It is okay to feel lost sometimes. What makes you happy when you are sad?
I like to play outside with my dog. But I am inside now.
That sounds like a good plan. Would you like to go play now?

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why are mountains so tall?
The ground under them pushes up slowly. Do you like to climb them?
Why do we see them so clearly?
They are far away and often dry.
Why do people go to the top?
The view is great from up there. Do you like looking down?
Why does it get cold there?
The air is thinner and has less heat.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How can I tell if my chickens are happy?
Happy chickens usually make a soft singing sound when they are calm. Do you hear that sound?
I do hear them singing in the yard.
That is a good sign of contentment. Do you feed them fresh greens?
I give them lettuce and old bread.
Lettuce is fine, but bread is not very good for them. I do not know what else you should serve.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I woke up when the small hand was on six.
That is a good time to start. Did you eat breakfast?
Yes, I ate toast before the big hand moved to twelve.
Noon is a great time for a meal. Did you finish it all?
I did, and then I played in the park until the small hand hit three.
That sounds like fun. Did you enjoy the games?
I played until the sun went down, which is when the small hand is on six again.
The clock helps us know when the day ends. Was it a happy day?
Yes, it was a long day, and now I am tired as the hands move toward ten.
Rest well. Good night.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I am trying to ride my bike, but I keep falling.
Do not worry, it happens to everyone. Are you looking at the road or the ground?
I look at the ground because I am scared.
Look far ahead instead. Do you have a friend with you?
No, I am all alone in the yard.
You can practice near a wall for safety. Do you feel safe there?
That sounds good, I will try it.
Good luck, you will do fine.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I need to cross this river fast. The water looks high.
The water is deep. Do you have a boat?
No, I do not. I must go now.
Please wait, it is not safe. Is there a bridge nearby?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late for the wedding. The car is not here.
Oh no. Are you wearing your hat?
No, I left it at home. I am running.
Run fast. I hope you arrive on time.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I feel very scared about my big test tomorrow.
Taking a deep breath can help you feel calm. Are you worried about a specific topic?
Yes, I do not understand the math part at all.
It is okay to not know everything. Let us look at one simple problem together.
That sounds good, but I am still nervous.
You have studied hard, so trust yourself. Just give your best try.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I fixed the wobbly chair today! I am so happy.
That is great news! What did you use to fix it?
I used a screwdriver and some new screws. It was hard but fun.
Good work! Do you know why it wobbled before?
I do not know. I think the leg was loose.
A loose leg makes sense. Is it solid now?
Yes, it is very solid. I am proud of myself.
That is wonderful. How do you feel about sitting in it?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am so tired but cannot sleep.
A cool room helps. Do you like a dark room?
I have things to do tomorrow.
Try a short breath. Do you drink water at night?
My mind will not stop.
Count to ten slowly. Is it a big worry?
I must go now.
Good luck. Do you have a warm blanket?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I found the perfect blue shoes today!
That is wonderful news. What size are they?
They fit my feet perfectly.
That sounds like a great feel. Do you have money to buy them?
Yes, I saved my pocket money for this.
Saving is a smart way to get things. I am happy for you.
I am so excited to wear them to school.
School will be fun with new shoes. Can I see them?
Look, they have little white dots on them.
Those dots look very cute. You should be proud of yourself.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late. Where is my math book?
I do not see it. Did you put it in your bag?
No. I think I left it on the desk.
That is a good guess. Do you need help finding it?
Yes. But the bell is ringing. I must run.
Okay. I will help you look quickly. Run fast.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: Today I went to a party with many friends.
That sounds like so much fun. Did you dance?
I danced and ate a big cake.
Yum, that sounds delicious. Was the cake sweet?
Yes, it was very sweet and I loved it.
I am glad you had a happy day.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I found a new town with tall trees and a big lake. I am so happy to be here.
That sounds very nice. Do you like the quiet sounds?
Yes, I do. The air feels fresh and clean here.
Fresh air is always good. Is there a shop for snacks?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: My rod snapped and my fish got away. I am so mad.
That sounds like a bad break. I am sorry you feel that way. What kind of fish was it?
It was a big bass. I dropped my line too.
Bass are tricky to catch. Do you have a spare line with you?
No, I do not. I have to walk back to the car.
Walking might help you cool down. Did you see any other fish nearby?
Yes, but I do not want to fish. I just want to go home.
It is okay to take a break. I will sit here if you stay. Do you want some water?
Yes, please. Thank you for helping me calm down.
You are welcome.

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I need to learn a song for tomorrow but I am in a huge rush.
Deep breaths, friend. Do you have the sheet music handy?
It is a very fast song and I keep stumbling on the high notes.
Try humming the tune first to relax your voice. Is the song in a key that feels comfortable for you?
I think it is too high. I just want to stop it from sounding bad.
Practice slowly and you will sound much clearer. Would you like a simple exercise to warm up?
I am running late so I must go now, thank you.
Good luck with your practice.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why is the snow so soft?
It feels like a fluffy pillow. Do you like standing in it?
Yes, I love it. Why does it crunch under my feet?
The ice parts are hard. Does it sound like eating chips?
I guess so. Why is the ground white?
Snow covers everything below. Do you see any brown leaves?
I see some brown spots. Why does it melt in my hand?
Your body is warm. It turns back into water.
I see water now. Why do you like snow?
I like how it makes things quiet. Do you think it is pretty?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I bake cookies for my sister?
Do you like chocolate? You mix the dough, scoop it, and bake at 375.
Yes, I love chocolate. What tools do I need?
I do not know all tools, but you need bowls and an oven. Is your oven big?
It is small. How long do I bake them?
You bake for ten to twelve minutes. Do you have a timer?
I do not have a timer. How do I know when they are done?
Look for brown edges. Are they soft in the middle?
They look brown. Should I take them out now?
Yes, take them out and let them cool.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: Look at my drawing. It is a big red house.
Wow, that looks really fun. Did you use new crayons?
Yes, my mom bought them yesterday. I am so happy I can draw again.
That is great news. You should frame it.
No, I want to give it to my teacher. She will love the color.
Your teacher will be very proud. What else is in the picture?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I have a very long flight to take soon. I am worried about getting stiff and sore.
That is a common worry. Do you have any special treats packed for the trip?
I have some chocolate bars. What else should I do to stay comfortable?
Please stretch your legs often. Is there a movie you want to watch?
I like action movies. What can I do to stop feeling thirsty?
Drink water before you get on the plane. Do you usually sleep well on planes?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I need a spot for my tent, please tell me fast.
Look for flat ground with no rocks. Is it dry there?
It looks wet, can I still use it?
Wet ground is bad for sleeping. Do you have a pad?
No pad, just a bag. What do I do now?
You must move if it is wet. Do you see dry grass?
Yes, there is grass. Is that okay?
Yes, that is a good choice.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I found a blue button on the floor today.
That is a nice find. What did you do with it?
I put it in my pocket and went to lunch.
A good place to keep it safe.
The soup was very hot and spilled on my shoe.
Oh no, that is not fun. Is your foot okay?
Yes, but now the shoe has a brown spot.
I do not know how to fix that. Let us just dry it out together.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I went to the pool today and tried to float on my back.
That is brave of you. Did you stay dry?
I got a little wet, but I made it across the lane.
Well done. Do you like the water now?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I am so mad. My sandwich fell in the dirt.
That is very sad. I am sorry. What was in the sandwich?
It had cheese and lettuce. Now it is all gone.
That is a huge loss. Do you want to get another one?
I do not want to get another. I want to go home.
That is a fair choice. Do you want my help with that?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: The boats look so big. I do not know where to walk.
Try the long path on the left. Do you like the sound of the waves?
I am stuck here. The boat is not going to move.
Yes, it is very still. Are you waiting for a friend?
I do not know what to do with my time.
You can sit on the bench and watch. Is the sun warm today?

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I am very hungry, but I do not know what to eat.
That is a tricky choice. Do you want something hot or cold?
I think I would like something warm and filling.
A big bowl of soup might be great for you. Would you like to add some bread?
That sounds good, but I am not sure I have enough space for bread.
You can always share the bread later. Do you like meat or just plants in your soup?
I think I will just have the plant soup for now.
That is a healthy choice. I hope it tastes nice to you.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: It was seven o'clock when I woke up.
That is an early start. Did you eat breakfast?
Yes, I had toast at eight.
Toast is a good choice. Do you like it with jam?
I went to the park at ten.
The park is a nice place to play. What did you see there?
I saw the sun set at six.
That must have looked very pretty.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I read my favorite book today. It has a big dragon on the cover.
That sounds fun. Do you like dragons?
Yes, I do. I also ate a warm apple pie after reading.
Apples are sweet. Was the pie hot?
It was very hot. I burned my tongue a little bit.
Oh no. Did you drink some cool milk?
Yes, I did. I am happy now and ready for sleep.
Good night. Sleep well.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I want to go camping. What do I need?
You need a tent, a bag, and food. Do you like to cook outside?
Yes, I love making fire.
Great. You need sticks and matches too. What kind of food do you like to make?
I like hot dogs.
Hot dogs are easy. Bring them in a bag. Do you have a tent?

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: Is the big fruit stall open?
Yes, it is open. Are you looking for anything sweet?
I want an apple, but where do I pay?
You pay the lady at the table. Do you have your coins ready?
Do they sell red apples or green ones?
They sell both red and green ones. Which color do you like best?
I like the red ones, so I will go there.
Good choice. Have a nice day at the market.

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I tried again, but I do not know what to do next.
That is a hard time. What part feels the most stuck?
I just feel lost and tired.
It is okay to rest your mind for a bit.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I like this song because it makes me jump.
Jumping is fun! Do you jump alone?
No, I jump with my teddy bear.
That sounds sweet. What is the song about?
It is about a big red truck.
A truck song is cool. Is it loud or soft?
It is loud and I clap my hands.
Clapping helps you keep the beat. Do you know the words?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am late. My boss helped me fix my code.
That is very nice of him. Are you feeling better now?
Yes, I am free. Can I go?
Please go. Have a good day.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I want to learn a new language. It feels very hard.
You can start with simple words. Do you like animals?
Yes, I love dogs. How do I say dog?
In Spanish, it is "perro". Try saying it three times.

talk.situation: the person wants advice
exchanges: I am stuck on this block game. The red one will not fit.
That sounds tricky. Did you try turning it upside down?
No, I never thought of that. Why does the blue one spin?
The blue one spins because it is round. Can you push the red one down?
Yes, it went in with a click. I feel so happy.
Great job solving it. Do you want to try a harder one next?

talk.situation: the person is in a hurry
exchanges: I am running late but I forgot my camera.
Do you have a phone with a camera on it?
Yes, I do, but the picture is blurry.
Hold your phone with two hands to stop the shake.
Okay, I am out the door now.
Good luck, I hope you catch a great shot.

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I fix a flickering light?
First, unplug the lamp or turn off the power. Do you know where your breaker box is?
I think it is in the basement.
That is a good guess. Please do not touch any wires if you are not sure. Do you feel safe doing this alone?
No, I am a bit scared.
That is okay to be careful. I do not know your specific house setup. Would you like me to call a pro?
Yes, please help me find one.
I can search for local electricians for you. Are they open right now?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: The wind was very loud today. My tree is bent over.
That sounds scary but safe. Are you okay?
Yes, I am inside and warm. I ate some soup.
That is a good plan for a storm. Was the soup hot?
It was very hot and yummy. Now the rain has stopped.
I am glad you are well. The sun is out now.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do circles have no corners?
Because the line never stops or turns. Do you like round things?
Yes, I do. Why do squares have four corners?
Because the lines stop and turn to make a box. Are your hands square?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I climbed a big hill and my legs hurt so much.
That sounds tiring. Are you sitting down to rest?
Yes, but I miss the top.
The top is waiting for you. Do you see any clouds?
The view was beautiful, but I am still sad.
It is okay to feel sad. Your heart is heavy.
I just want to go home now.
Going home is a good choice.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I found a cool rock in my garden.
That is great! Is it smooth or bumpy?
It is very smooth and gray.
You must be a good finder. Do you keep them in a box?
Yes, I have a whole box full of rocks.
That is a nice collection.

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: I like kicking the ball really hard.
That is fun to do. Do you aim for the goal?
Yes, I want to score a point.
Good luck with that. Is your team winning today?
We have one goal and they have none.
You are leading the game. How many players are on your team?
There are eleven players on each side.
That makes a full team. Do you like playing goalie or forward?
I like running fast and shooting the ball.
Running fast is exciting.

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I feel sad because my house in the small village is gone.
I am sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it?
I miss the quiet streets and the old trees.
That is a very peaceful place. What did you like best there?
I do not have that now. I feel lost.
That is a hard feeling. I do not know how to fix it, but I am here.
At least the kind people still remember me.
That is a good thing. Is there anything else on your mind?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I hate this rain. It is making me feel sad.
Sorry you are sad. Do you want to sit by the window?
No, I want to play outside.
The rain will stop soon. Do you like looking for ducks?
I like ducks, but I am stuck inside.
Let us play a game while we wait. Do you have a favorite toy?

talk.situation: the person is a child
exchanges: Why is the water so blue today?
The sun is making it shine. Do you see the big boats?
Yes, they look like big sleeping cats.
That is a nice way to say it. Do you hear the waves crashing?
It sounds like a giant washing the rocks.
You have a very good ear. Would you like to feed the seagulls?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: I passed my driving test today! It feels great.
That is wonderful news. Do you feel safe in the car?
Yes, I feel very calm now.
I am glad to hear that. Have you picked a favorite song for the drive?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: How do I keep my fish healthy?
You must change the water every week. Is your tank big enough?
What should I feed them?
Small flakes or pellets work best. Do you have a special feeder?
Why is my water cloudy?
That is often new dirt or bacteria. Is it white or yellow?
How do I clean the glass?
Use a soft pad to scrape the algae. Do you have one yet?
I want to add another fish.
I do not know your tank size. Can you check the space?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: The lights went out. How do I keep my food cold?
Keep the door shut tight to keep the cold in. Do you have a thermometer inside?
No, just my hands. Do I need to worry about the freezer?
It should stay cold for a long time if you do not open it. Is your freezer full or empty?

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I am so late for school. I missed the bus.
Oh no, that sounds bad. Did you run?
Yes, I ran all the way. My legs hurt.
That is brave. Are you safe now?
Yes, I made it to the door. Phew.
Great job. Do you have time for a snack?

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: Look at the big clock on the wall.
It is a shiny clock. Does it make a loud sound?
Yes, it ticks every second. I like the sound.
Ticking is nice. Do you know what time it is?
It is one o'clock. The short hand points to one.
One o'clock is early. Do you have plans for today?
I will play with my toys soon.
That sounds fun. Which toy will you play with first?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I cannot put the last piece in. I am so mad.
Take a deep breath. It will come soon. Do you see where it fits?
I tried that spot twice. It does not go.
That is hard work. Let us try a new spot. Are the colors matching?
The edges look wrong. Maybe I broke it.
You did not break it. We just need to look closer. Do you see a tiny line?
Wait. I see it now. It is upside down.
Yes, you found it. You are smart. How do you feel now?
I feel good. Thank you for helping.
I am happy for you. You did the work.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: I am not sure if I should say thank you when someone helps me pick up my dropped toy.
Yes, you should always say thank you. Do you think a small smile helps too?
I think a smile is nice. What if I forget to say it?
If you forget, just say it when you remember. Do you feel better now that you know?

talk.situation: the person wants to learn how to do something
exchanges: I want to know the order of the months.
That is a fun thing to learn. Do you know what month comes after January?
I think it is February.
Yes, that is right. Tell me, do you remember what comes after February?
I am not sure about that one.
That is okay to not know. It is March, and you will learn it soon.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: My chair leg is wobbly and it hurts my back.
That sounds bad. Did you try to tighten it?
I tried, but I do not have the right tool.
That is tricky. Do you have a screwdriver nearby?
No, I only have a fork and some tape.
Do not use tape on the wood. It will not hold.
So what should I do now?
Go to a shop to get a real tool.
Okay, I will go there after lunch.
That is a good plan. Hope it feels better soon.

talk.situation: the person is telling a small story about their day
exchanges: I dropped my cup on the floor. It broke into three pieces.
Oh no, that is a shame. Did you get hurt?
No, I am fine. I saw a cat run under the table right before.
That is very interesting. Was the cat scared?
Yes, it looked at me with big eyes. Then I stepped on a piece of the cup.
ouch, that must hurt. Be careful next time.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why is it hard to read at night?
Your eyes get tired in the dark. Do you like reading under a lamp?
I do, but it still feels sleepy.
Tired eyes want to close fast. I do not know why you feel that way.

talk.situation: the person has a question
exchanges: What do I need to bring to a campsite?
You need a tent, a bag for sleeping, and food. Is this your first time camping?
Do I need to bring my own water?
Yes, pack enough water for drinking and cooking. Do you know where you are going?
How do I light the campfire?
I do not know the exact rules for that area. Please check the local guide.

talk.situation: the person is curious and asks why
exchanges: Why do bears sleep in the winter?
They are cold, so they hide in a hole to stay warm. Do you like cold nights?
I do not. Why are snakes happy without legs?
Sliding is easy for them on the ground. Do you like to slide down hills?
Yes. Why do lions roar so loud?
It tells other animals, I am here. Do you have a big voice?
No, it is small. Why do birds fly away from storms?
The wind is too strong for their small wings. Do you like storms?
No, I do not. Why do rabbits eat grass?
It is their main food to keep them strong. Do you have a pet?

talk.situation: the person is unsure what to do
exchanges: I have a small robot that stopped moving. I do not know what is wrong with it.
Did you check if the batteries are full? Sometimes they just need new power.
The batteries look full, but it makes a strange noise. What should I do now?
That is a tricky sound. Have you tried turning it off and on again?

talk.situation: the person is a little upset
exchanges: I fell off my bike and now I hurt my knee. It hurts so much.
That sounds like it really hurts. Is the skin broken?
No, it is just a bruise. I do not want to ride again.
It is ok to rest for now. Do you like your bike?
Yes, I do. I just got scared and cannot stop crying.
It is safe to feel sad. We can wait until you feel better.

talk.situation: the person is happy and wants to share it
exchanges: Look at this small green island! It looks so fun.
Wow, it is very pretty. What is your favorite part there?
The warm sand feels nice. I want to build a big fort.
That sounds like great fun. Do you have any toys to bring?
Yes, I packed a red bucket and a shovel. I am so happy to be here.
